```{r setup, include=FALSE}
extrafont::loadfonts(quiet = TRUE)

# ── Register EB Garamond with R's graphics device ────────────────────────
# CSS alone cannot reach text rendered into ggplot SVG/PNG output. We
# register EB Garamond with R's font registry so any
# `family = "EB Garamond"` ggplot/ggiraph call renders correctly.
#
# Two-tier strategy (both defensive, both no-op cleanly if unavailable):
#   1. systemfonts::register_variant — aliases "EB Garamond" to an
#      installed serif so R has metrics for layout. ggiraph still emits
#      font-family="EB Garamond" in the SVG and the browser pairs it
#      with the Google Fonts webfont loaded via www/cssloaders.html.
#   2. showtext (optional) — if installed, also pull the real Google
#      Font so static raster output looks correct.
local({
  if (requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
    have_eb <- "EB Garamond" %in% systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
    if (!have_eb) {
      candidates <- c("Garamond", "EB Garamond", "Georgia", "Times New Roman", "serif")
      installed  <- systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
      fallback   <- candidates[candidates %in% installed][1]
      if (!is.na(fallback)) {
        try(systemfonts::register_variant(
          name   = "EB Garamond",
          family = fallback
        ), silent = TRUE)
      }
    }
  }
  if (requireNamespace("showtext", quietly = TRUE) &&
      requireNamespace("sysfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
    if (!"EB Garamond" %in% sysfonts::font_families()) {
      try(sysfonts::font_add_google("EB Garamond", "EB Garamond"),
          silent = TRUE)
    }
    try({
      showtext::showtext_auto()
      showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = 96)
    }, silent = TRUE)
  }
})

# ── Self-contained download icon ─────────────────────────────────────
# Shiny's downloadButton() defaults to a Font Awesome glyph
# (<i class="fa fa-download">). When the FA webfont fails to load, that
# glyph renders as a blank tofu square. dl_icon() supplies an inline SVG
# instead, wrapped in an <i> tag so it passes Shiny's validateIcon()
# check (which requires the icon tag name to be "i"). This removes the
# webfont dependency entirely, so the download affordance always renders.
dl_icon <- function() {
  tags$i(
    class = "dl-svg-icon", `aria-hidden` = "true",
    HTML(paste0(
      '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" ',
      'width="1em" height="1em" focusable="false" ',
      'style="vertical-align:-0.125em;margin-right:0.45em;fill:currentColor;">',
      '<path d="M8 1.5a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v6.69l2.22-2.22a.75.75 0 1 1 ',
      '1.06 1.06l-3.5 3.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06 0l-3.5-3.5a.75.75 0 1 1 ',
      '1.06-1.06l2.22 2.22V2.25A.75.75 0 0 1 8 1.5Z"/>',
      '<path d="M2.5 10.75a.75.75 0 0 0-1.5 0v1.75A1.75 1.75 0 0 0 2.75 ',
      '14.25h10.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 0 15 12.5v-1.75a.75.75 0 0 0-1.5 0v1.75a',
      '.25.25 0 0 1-.25.25H2.75a.25.25 0 0 1-.25-.25Z"/></svg>'
    ))
  )
}

east_coast_states_to_relocate <- c("RI", "DE", "DC", "MD")

us_states <- readRDS(here::here("data", "final", "us_states.Rds"))

#us_states <- states(cb = TRUE, resolution = "20m") %>%
  #shift_geometry() %>%
  #sf::st_cast("MULTIPOLYGON") %>% 
  #select(GEOID, ABBR = STUSPS, NAME, geometry)

us_states <- us_states %>% 
  left_join(
    us_states %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      bind_cols(
        us_states %>%
          sf::st_centroid() %>%
          sf::st_coordinates() %>% 
          as_tibble()
      )
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    x_lab = case_when(
      ABBR %in% east_coast_states_to_relocate ~ 2300000,
      ABBR == "FL" ~ X + 80000,
      ABBR == "LA" ~ X - 60000,
      .default = X
    ),
    y_lab = case_when(
      ABBR == "DC" ~ Y - 180000,
      ABBR == "DE" ~ Y + 100000,
      ABBR == "NH" ~ Y - 40000,
      ABBR == "VT" ~ Y + 40000,
      ABBR == "MD" ~ Y - 40000,
      ABBR == "LA" ~ Y + 40000,
      .default = Y
    )
  ) %>% 
  left_join(national_data)

### ----- Script sourcing helper -----
# Bare source() on a file missing from the deployment bundle fails with the
# opaque message "cannot open the connection", which says nothing about WHICH
# file is absent. On shinyapps.io that surfaces only as a stack trace in the
# logs. This helper checks first and names the offending path, along with the
# reason it is almost always missing: the file is not declared in the
# `resource_files:` block of this document's YAML header, so rsconnect never
# uploaded it. Run scripts/preflight_deploy.R before deploying to catch this
# locally instead of in production.
#
# `envir` must be an ENVIRONMENT, not TRUE/FALSE. Passing local = TRUE from
# inside this helper would evaluate the sourced file in the helper's own frame,
# and every object it defines would be discarded on return. Defaulting to
# parent.frame() reproduces what a top-level `source(..., local = TRUE)` does:
# evaluate in the caller's environment (here, the setup chunk).
source_required <- function(..., envir = parent.frame()) {
  path <- here::here(...)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop(
      "Required script not found: ", path, "\n",
      "  If the app works locally but fails after deploy, this file is ",
      "probably missing from the `resource_files:` list in the YAML header ",
      "of ADA_PARC.Rmd. Add it, then redeploy.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  source(path, local = envir)
}

### ----- Functions import -----

source_required("scripts", "functions.R")

### ----- Tier palette import -----
# scripts/palettes.R is the single source of truth for ADA-PARC tier colour.
# Sourced into the GLOBAL environment (envir = globalenv()) rather than locally,
# because ADA_PARC_PALETTE and the pal_* accessors are read from inside Shiny
# reactives and render functions that do not share this chunk's environment.
# Nothing below should carry a tier hex literal. See docs/color-palette-expansion.qmd.
source_required("scripts", "palettes.R", envir = globalenv())

# The blue and slate chrome accent used to be patched in here, after
# palettes.R had been sourced, because palettes.R was shared with a second,
# still maroon copy of this document and could not be edited for one of them.
# That copy is gone and this document is canon, so the four tokens
# (ui_accent, ui_accent_dark, attr_text, attr_rule) now live in the standard
# set in scripts/palettes.R. Do not reintroduce a runtime override: values
# there are verified by `python3 scripts/check_palette.py` and mirrored in the
# fallback :root of www/styles.css, and a patch applied here is visible to
# neither.

### ----- Fixed city/place map classification -----
# City tract choropleth (output$snapshotmap) previously recomputed its color
# scale PER CITY (colorQuantile if >=4 tracts had data, else colorNumeric).
# That broke down for the many small/rural places with <4 tracts: 1-3 tract
# cities either got a non-4-step legend (colorNumeric + addLegend's default
# pretty()-based binning) or, for single-tract places, a blank legend (the
# domain collapses to one value, so addLegend's auto-computed cuts have
# length <= 1). See project memory "City Map Small-N Legend Bug".
#
# Fix: compute ONE fixed 4-category classification from the full national
# tract distribution (reusing the same create_non_overlapping_buckets() /
# format_ranges() helpers already used for the national state map), so every
# city's map is classified against the same breakpoints regardless of how
# many tracts that city has. This also makes colors comparable across
# different cities' maps, which per-city quantiles never allowed.
city_map_breaks <- create_non_overlapping_buckets(tracts_data$pct_cni_total_dis_place)
city_map_labels <- format_ranges(city_map_breaks, "pct_cni_total_dis_place")
```

# Home

```{r home}
# Embed logo as base64 data URI so the src resolves independently of Shiny's
# session URL context (relative paths like "PARC_blue_icon.png" can 404 when
# the browser resolves them against /session/ID/... rather than the app root).
#
# BRAND (provisional, 2026-08-04): www/brand holds the new identity pending
# approval from the ADA centers. Two blue-on-transparent files pair with two
# white-on-transparent files for dark surfaces:
#   PARC_blue_icon.png  / PARC_white_icon.png  384x384 square mark
#   PARC_blue_text.png  / PARC_white_text.png  448x264 two-line wordmark
# The hero carries both marks, mirroring the fact sheet banner adopted
# 2026-08-04 (fs_header() in factsheets/_generate/R/factsheet-functions.R):
# icon left, title block centred, wordmark right. The hero previously used the
# icon alone on the reasoning that the wordmark only repeats what the
# "Welcome to ADA-PARC" heading says; that was true of the words but not of
# the composition, and the home page and the fact sheets now open the same
# way. The BLUE files are used here, not the white ones, because the hero sits
# on the white page rather than on the navy banner.
logo_uri <- base64enc::dataURI(
  file = here::here("www", "brand", "PARC_blue_icon.png"),
  mime = "image/png"
)
wordmark_uri <- base64enc::dataURI(
  file = here::here("www", "brand", "PARC_blue_text.png"),
  mime = "image/png"
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* EB Garamond: declared here because shinyApp() sub-apps run in an
         isolated context where the parent flexdashboard www/styles.css
         does not reliably cascade into the rendered content. */
      *, *::before, *::after {
        box-sizing: border-box;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
      }
      /* ROOT FONT SIZE — read this before touching any rem value below.
         fluidPage() loads Bootstrap 3, whose scaffolding sets
         `html { font-size: 10px }`. Every rem on this page therefore
         resolved against a 10px root, which rendered 1.4rem body copy at
         14px and the contact line at 10.5px, roughly 62% of the intended
         size and well under the site's accessibility floor. Pinning the
         root here makes rem deterministic regardless of what Bootstrap
         version ships underneath, and every size below is expressed in
         rem against this 16px base (1.3125rem = 21px, matching the
         body size set in www/styles.css for the rest of the site). */
      html {
        font-size: 16px;
      }
      body, html {
        height: 100%;
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        overflow-x: hidden;
        /* `auto`, not `scroll`: `scroll` paints a permanent scrollbar track
           even when the content fits. */
        overflow-y: auto;
        background: #f5f7fa;
      }
      .main-content {
        padding: 2.5rem 2.75rem 3rem 2.75rem;
        width: 100%;
        max-width: 1020px;
        margin: 0 auto;
        background: #ffffff;
        border-left: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-right: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        min-height: 100vh;
      }

      /* ---- Hero ---- */
      /* Three-column grid, matching .factsheet-header: mark left, title block
         centred, wordmark right. `auto 1fr auto` is what makes the middle
         column centre against the PAGE rather than against the space left
         over between the two marks, provided the two side columns end up
         near enough the same width. They do: the 72px square icon and the
         wordmark set to 60px tall on a 448x264 file (~102px wide) differ by
         about 30px, which is not readable as an offset at this width. A flex
         row with `flex: 1` on the text block, which is what this replaced,
         cannot centre at all: it centres the text inside whatever width is
         left, so the heading drifts left as the wordmark grows. */
      .home-hero {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 1.5rem;
        padding: 1.25rem 0 1.125rem 0;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 1.75rem;
      }
      .home-logo-wrap {
        flex-shrink: 0;
      }
      /* The brand icon is a 1:1 square, unlike the old wordmark it replaced,
         so height rather than width is the constraint that sets its visual
         weight. 72px reads level with the 32px hero heading; the old 96x64
         box would have shrunk a square mark to 64px and left it sitting
         light against the type. */
      .home-logo-wrap img {
        width: 72px;
        height: 72px;
        display: block;
      }
      /* Sized by HEIGHT, as on the fact sheet banner, so the two marks share
         an optical baseline. A width rule would set the height by accident,
         since the two files have different aspect ratios. */
      .home-wordmark {
        height: 60px;
        width: auto;
        display: block;
      }
      .hero-text-block {
        text-align: center;
        min-width: 0;
      }
      .welcome-text {
        font-size: 2rem;     /* 32px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.3rem 0;
        line-height: 1.15;
      }
      /* 19px, down from 20px. Below the 21px site body size, but this is a
         one-line standfirst under a 32px heading rather than reading copy,
         and it stays well clear of the 16px floor. #1c1c1c on #ffffff is
         17.4:1. */
      .welcome-sub {
        font-size: 1.1875rem; /* 19px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.4;
        margin: 0;
      }

      /* ---- Nav Cards ---- */
      /* Two columns, so four cards sit as a 2x2 block. Each card is wider
         than it was at three across, which is what lets the titles and
         descriptions carry the larger type without wrapping awkwardly. */
      .nav-cards {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
        gap: 1.125rem;
        margin-bottom: 2rem;
      }
      .nav-card {
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-top: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
        border-radius: 0 0 6px 6px;
        padding: 1.375rem 1.375rem 1.25rem 1.375rem;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        /* Centred, matching the hero above. `align-items: center` is what
           centres the icon tile and the button, which are flex ITEMS and so
           are unaffected by text-align; text-align centres the title and the
           description, which are text inside full-width items. Both rules
           are needed, and neither substitutes for the other. */
        align-items: center;
        text-align: center;
        transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease, transform 0.15s ease;
      }
      .nav-card:hover {
        box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(28,43,58,0.12);
        transform: translateY(-2px);
      }
      /* Tile tint is #eef3fa, the palest usable step of the brand navy,
         replacing the maroon tint #fdf5f5 that paired with the old stroke.
         Not pure white: the card itself is white, so a white tile would
         erase the tile and leave the glyph floating. #eef3fa is 1.06:1
         against the card, enough to read as a shape, while the #013176
         stroke on it measures 11.07:1, comfortably past the 3:1 that
         non-text graphics require and past the 4.5:1 text floor as well. */
      .nav-card-icon {
        width: 50px;
        height: 50px;
        background: #eef3fa;
        border-radius: 8px;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        margin-bottom: 1rem;
        flex-shrink: 0;
      }
      .nav-card-icon svg {
        width: 26px;
        height: 26px;
        fill: none;
        stroke: #013176;
        stroke-width: 2;
        stroke-linecap: round;
        stroke-linejoin: round;
      }
      .nav-card-title {
        font-size: 1.3125rem;   /* 21px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
        line-height: 1.25;
      }
      .nav-card-desc {
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        flex-grow: 1;
      }
      /* Brand navy #013176, sampled from the tile fill of the PARC icon and
         defined as --brand-navy in factsheets/_generate/assets/factsheet-base.css.
         The jump-ahead buttons carry the identity colour rather than maroon so
         the one interactive element on the page is the one thing wearing the
         mark's blue; maroon stays on the structural rules (card top border,
         hero underline) and on the card icons. Hard-coded rather than
         referenced because this sub-app runs in an isolated shinyApp() context
         that the parent stylesheet's custom properties do not reach; if the
         approved brand shifts the blue, this literal and --brand-navy must
         move together.
         #ffffff on #013176 is 12.34:1. */
      .nav-card-btn {
        display: inline-block;
        padding: 0.55rem 1.2rem;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        background-color: #013176;
        border-radius: 4px;
        text-decoration: none !important;
        letter-spacing: 0.02em;
        transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
        cursor: pointer;
        border: none;
      }
      /* Gold on the darker blue is 6.6:1, so the hover state clears AA for
         normal text and does not depend on the 17px weight to pass. */
      .nav-card-btn:hover {
        background-color: #01214f;
        color: #C9A428 !important;
      }

      /* ---- Callout (full-width) ---- */
      .callout-full {
        border-left: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
        background: #f9f7f4;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 2rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .callout-label {
        font-size: 1rem;        /* 16px, uppercase with tracking */
        font-weight: 700;
        letter-spacing: 0.1em;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
      }
      .callout-text {
        font-size: 1.1875rem;   /* 19px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        font-weight: 500;
        margin: 0;
      }

      /* ---- Single-column sections ---- */
      .home-section {
        padding-bottom: 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 1.5rem;
        border-bottom: 0.5px solid #e4e8ef;
      }
      .home-section:last-of-type {
        border-bottom: none;
        margin-bottom: 0;
        padding-bottom: 0;
      }
      .sec-heading {
        font-size: 1.5rem;      /* 24px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.6rem 0;
        line-height: 1.25;
        border-left: 3px solid #1c2b3a;
        padding-left: 0.7rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .sec-body {
        font-size: 1.1875rem;   /* 19px */
        color: #2d3748;
        line-height: 1.7;
        margin: 0;
      }
      .sec-sub {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-bottom: 0.6rem;
      }

      /* ---- Regions Grid ---- */
      .regions-grid {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
        gap: 0.2rem 2rem;
        margin: 0.75rem 0;
        list-style: none;
        padding: 0;
      }
      .regions-grid li {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        color: #2d3748;
        line-height: 1.55;
        padding: 4px 0;
      }
      .region-num {
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-right: 5px;
      }

      /* ---- Bottom Bar ---- */
      .bottom-bar {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
        gap: 1.75rem;
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1.5px solid #dfe3e9;
        border-radius: 6px;
        padding: 1.375rem 1.5rem;
        margin-top: 2rem;
      }
      .bottom-col-title {
        font-size: 1.25rem;     /* 20px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
        line-height: 1.25;
        border-left: 3px solid #1c2b3a;
        padding-left: 0.55rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .bottom-col-body {
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        color: #333333;
        line-height: 1.65;
      }
      /* Lead line of the authorship column, so the current maintainer reads
         as the primary credit and the historical contributors sit under it. */
      .bottom-col-lead {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        line-height: 1.65;
      }
      .bottom-col-note {
        font-size: 1rem;        /* 16px */
        color: #333333;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-top: 0.2rem;
      }
      .bottom-col-body a {
        color: #1c2b3a;
        text-decoration: underline;
      }
      .email-button {
        display: inline-block;
        padding: 0.5rem 1.2rem;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        font-weight: 600;
        color: white !important;
        background-color: #013176;
        border-radius: 4px;
        text-decoration: none !important;
        margin: 0.6rem 0 0.5rem 0;
        letter-spacing: 0.02em;
        transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
      }
      .email-button:hover {
        background-color: #01214f;
        text-decoration: none !important;
      }
      .questions-contact {
        font-size: 1rem;        /* 16px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
      }

      /* Narrow desktop and tablet: keep the 2x2 card block until the cards
         would be too tight to hold a title on one line. */
      @media (max-width: 780px) {
        .main-content { padding: 2rem 1.75rem 2.5rem 1.75rem; }
        .nav-cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
        .bottom-bar { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
      }

      @media (max-width: 640px) {
        .main-content { padding: 1.5rem 1.25rem 2rem 1.25rem; }
        /* Stacked hero: the marks are grid items, not inline content, so
           text-align cannot centre them. justify-self can. */
        .home-hero { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 0.85rem; text-align: center; }
        .home-logo-wrap, .home-wordmark { justify-self: center; }
        .regions-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
        .welcome-text { font-size: 1.75rem; }  /* 28px */
        .sec-heading { font-size: 1.3125rem; } /* 21px */
      }
    "))
  ),

  div(class = "main-content",

      # Hero
      # Icon carries alt="" because the wordmark to its right already names
      # the centre, and the heading names it a third time; announcing the
      # mark here would make a screen reader say "ADA-PARC" three times
      # before the first sentence of the page.
      div(class = "home-hero",
        div(class = "home-logo-wrap",
          tags$img(src = logo_uri, alt = "")
        ),
        div(class = "hero-text-block",
          div(class = "welcome-text", "Welcome to ADA-PARC"),
          div(class = "welcome-sub", "Tracking disability participation across the United States")
        ),
        tags$img(class = "home-wordmark", src = wordmark_uri, alt = "ADA-PARC")
      ),

      # Navigation script: from the Home nav cards, jump to a top-level
      # flexdashboard page.
      #
      # Home renders as an embedded shinyApp(), so this code runs inside an
      # iframe that does not contain the navbar. Three paths are tried in
      # order, each independent of the last:
      #
      #   1. Direct: reach top.document and drive the navbar link. Only
      #      possible when parent and frame share an origin; throws otherwise.
      #   2. postMessage: hand the request to the listener installed in
      #      www/cssloaders.html, which runs in the document that owns the
      #      navbar. Works regardless of origin. This is the path that was
      #      missing, and the reason the cards did nothing.
      #   3. Hash: last resort, same-origin only.
      #
      # Every selector is scoped to the top navbar (.navbar-nav), so inner
      # tabsets such as the Scorecards tabset, and the scorecard/factsheet
      # iframes, can never be targeted by mistake.
      tags$script(HTML("
window.adaparcNavigateToTab = function(page) {
  var slugs = {
    'Home':          'home',
    'National Data': 'national-data',
    'City Data':     'city-data',
    'Scorecards':    'scorecards',
    'Scorecard':     'scorecards',
    'Fact Sheets':   'fact-sheets',
    'Help':          'help'
  };
  var slug = slugs[page];

  /* 1) Same-origin direct path. Any cross-origin access throws, which is
        caught here so the postMessage path below still runs. */
  try {
    var doc = top.document;
    void doc.documentElement;
    if (typeof top.adaparcShowPage === 'function') {
      if (top.adaparcShowPage(page)) { return true; }
    }
    if (slug) {
      var byHref = doc.querySelectorAll('.navbar-nav a[href$=\\'#' + slug + '\\']');
      if (byHref.length) { byHref[0].click(); return true; }
    }
    var links = doc.querySelectorAll('.navbar-nav a');
    for (var i = 0; i < links.length; i++) {
      if ((links[i].textContent || '').trim() === page) { links[i].click(); return true; }
    }
  } catch (e) { /* fall through to postMessage */ }

  /* 2) Cross-origin safe path. The listener lives in www/cssloaders.html. */
  try {
    var target = (window.parent && window.parent !== window) ? window.parent : top;
    target.postMessage({ adaparc: 'navigate', page: page }, '*');
    return true;
  } catch (e) {}

  /* 3) Last resort. */
  if (slug) {
    try { top.location.hash = '#' + slug; return true; } catch (e) {}
  }
  return false;
};
      ")),

      # Navigation Cards
      div(class = "nav-cards",

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9 20L3 17V4l6 3m0 13l6-3m-6 3V7m6 10l6 3V7l-6-3m0 13V7M9 7l6-3"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "National Data"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "Examine national and state-level patterns for people with disabilities."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to National Data",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('National Data');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        ),

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="3" y="8" width="5" height="13"/><rect x="9.5" y="3" width="5" height="18"/><rect x="16" y="11" width="5" height="10"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "City Data"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "Investigate disability statistics at the municipal and city level."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to City Data",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('City Data');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        ),

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9 5H7a2 2 0 00-2 2v12a2 2 0 002 2h10a2 2 0 002-2V7a2 2 0 00-2-2h-2M9 5a2 2 0 002 2h2a2 2 0 002-2M9 5a2 2 0 012-2h2a2 2 0 012 2m-6 9l2 2 4-4"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "Scorecards"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "View state-by-state report cards across each disability domain."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to Scorecards",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('Scorecards');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        ),

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M14 3H7a2 2 0 00-2 2v14a2 2 0 002 2h10a2 2 0 002-2V8l-5-5z"/><path d="M14 3v5h5"/><path d="M9 13h6M9 17h6"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "Fact Sheets"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "Read short, plain-language briefs on single disability outcomes."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to Fact Sheets",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('Fact Sheets');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        )

      ),

      # Did You Know callout \u2014 full width
      div(class = "callout-full",
        div(class = "callout-label", "Did you know"),
        tags$p(class = "callout-text",
          "Nationally, between the ages of 18 to 64, 1 in 4 individuals with a disability live below the poverty line."
        )
      ),

      # Single-column sections
      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "What is the ADA?"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), established in 1990, is a landmark civil rights law that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life.",
          " Since the ADA, organizations across public and private sectors have worked to improve the quality of life for individuals with disabilities in the U.S. ADA-PARC emphasizes key components of Census and HUD data to shed light on the lived experiences and outcomes for people with disabilities."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "Work of the ADA-PARC"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "The ADA-PARC has research teams focused on Community Living, Community Participation, and Work/Economic Participation measures, using Regional Steering Committees in each of the ten participating regions to gather and review appropriate data.",
          " The intent of this effort is to inform ADA Center technical assistance and to help community-level stakeholders increase participation opportunities in their communities."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "About the ADA-PARC"),
        div(class = "sec-sub",
          "A collaborative research project of ten ADA Regional Centers:"
        ),
        tags$ul(
          class = "regions-grid",
          role = "list",
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">1.</span> New England')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">2.</span> Northeast')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">3.</span> Mid-Atlantic')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">4.</span> Southeast')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">5.</span> Great Lakes')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">6.</span> Southwest')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">7.</span> Great Plains')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">8.</span> Rocky Mountain')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">9.</span> Pacific')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">10.</span> Northwest'))
        ),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "Collaborating institutions include the ADA Knowledge Translation Center, TIRR Memorial Hermann, Syracuse University, and the University of Illinois at Chicago."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "Purpose of this website"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "The ADA-PARC website presents public data that illuminates the status of people with disabilities in local communities, including national, state, county, and city data.",
          " The three main data domains are Community Living, Community Participation, and Work & Economics, each presented in map and tabular form."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "Grant Information"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
```
