# National Data

```{r National Data}
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(shinycssloaders)
library(DT)
library(ggiraph)

# Pre-compute initial topic choices so the selector has a valid value on load
.initial_nat_choices <- dict_vars %>%
  filter(is_demographics == TRUE, !is.na(national_dropdown_label)) %>%
  select(national_dropdown_label, var_readable) %>%
  tibble::deframe() %>%
  names()
.initial_nat_selected <- if ("People with Disabilities" %in% .initial_nat_choices) {
  "People with Disabilities"
} else {
  .initial_nat_choices[1]
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* TABLE CONTAINER */
      .table-container {
        height: auto;
        max-height: none;
        min-height: 500px;
        overflow-y: visible;
        margin-bottom: 40px;
      }
      .table-container .dataTables_wrapper .dataTables_scrollBody {
        height: auto !important;
        max-height: none !important;
        overflow-y: visible !important;
      }

      /* Add space between map legend and table controls */
      .table-container .dataTables_wrapper {
        margin-top: 1rem;
        clear: both;
      }

      /* NATIONAL TABLE STYLING
         Roomier on-screen table (the downloadable report keeps its own,
         tighter print styling in national/national_topic.qmd).
         Selectors are written as table.dataTable.table_national so they
         outrank DataTables' own thead/tbody padding rules; a bare
         .table_national th loses that cascade and the padding is dropped. */
      .table_national {
        width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th {
        position: sticky;
        top: 0;
        background-color: #1c2b3a;
        color: #ffffff;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 19px;
        z-index: 1;
        white-space: normal;      /* allow wrapping */
        word-wrap: break-word;    /* wrap long words */
        /* Header row sits taller than the body rows: ~62px vs ~50px for a
           single line of text. Extra right padding keeps header labels clear
           of the sort arrows, which DataTables absolutely positions there. */
        padding: 18px 26px 18px 12px;
        line-height: 1.25;
        vertical-align: middle;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national tbody td {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 17px;
        white-space: nowrap;
        /* ~36px body row against the ~62px header, scaled back from a first
           pass that ran too roomy. Header left as is, so it keeps reading as
           clearly taller than the body rows. */
        padding: 7px 12px;
        line-height: 1.3;
        vertical-align: middle;
      }

      /* Right-align numeric cells; left-align State */
      table.dataTable.table_national tbody td {
        text-align: right;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national tbody td:first-child {
        text-align: left;
      }

      /* Remove extra space under h1 */
      h1 {
        margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
      }

      /* Intro text under National Data */
      .national-intro {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.75rem;
      }

      /* Map summary text */
      .map-summary {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
      }

      /* DataTables controls font */
      div.dataTables_wrapper,
      div.dataTables_wrapper label,
      div.dataTables_wrapper select,
      div.dataTables_wrapper input {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
      }

      /* Map / table section heading inside cards. Sized in px for the same
         Bootstrap 3 reason as the banner above: the old `1.9rem` resolved
         against a 10px root and rendered at 19px, barely larger than the
         17px body text around it. Shared by the map card and the table
         card so the two section headings stay the same weight. */
      .national-map-title {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 24px;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-bottom: 9px;
        margin-top: 3px;
        padding-bottom: 6px;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #1c2b3a;
      }

      /* Interpretation note under table title */
      .interpretation-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 17px;
        color: #000000;
        font-style: normal;
        margin-top: -0.25rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.75rem;
      }

      /* Standalone interpretation-note container shown above the map.
         Maroon accent + pale gold-tinted panel (design canon). Dark navy
         text on the pale panel keeps contrast well above WCAG AA at the
         17px minimum body size used across the site. */
      .map-interpretation-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 17px;
        line-height: 1.5;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        background: #faf5ec;
        border: 1px solid #e6d9bd;
        border-left: 5px solid #1c2b3a;
        border-radius: 6px;
        padding: 0.7rem 1rem;
        margin: 0.35rem 0 1rem 0;
      }
      .map-interpretation-note-label {
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
      }

      /* SelectInput controls styling */
      .shiny-input-container label {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-weight: 500;
      }
      select.form-control, .selectize-input {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 18px !important;
      }

      /* Leaflet legend styling */
      .leaflet-control-layers-list label {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 16px !important;
      }
      .info {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 16px !important;
        padding: 10px 15px;
        background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.95);
        border-radius: 5px;
        box-shadow: 0 0 15px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);
      }
      .info h4 {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 16px;
        margin: 0 0 5px 0;
        font-weight: 600;
      }
      .legend {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 17px !important;
      }
      .legend label {
        display: block;
        margin-bottom: 5px;
      }

      /* Source note below table */
      .national-source-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 16px;
        color: #444;
        margin-top: 0.75rem;
        margin-bottom: 1rem;
      }

      /* ── National controls panel ─────────────────────────────────────────
         One horizontal band: the two selectors on the left, the download on
         the right behind a full-height vertical rule. The topic summary lives
         in its own card below so nothing competes for width here. */
      .national-controls-split {
        display: flex;
        align-items: stretch;
        gap: 1.5rem;
      }

      /* Selector row: align-items:flex-start keeps the two labels on the same
         baseline. Bottom alignment used to push the shorter control down
         whenever a long topic name wrapped the second select box onto two
         lines. */
      .national-controls-row {
        flex: 1 1 auto;
        min-width: 0;
        display: flex;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
        align-items: flex-start;
        gap: 1.25rem;
      }
      .national-control-field {
        flex: 1 1 16rem;
        min-width: 0;
      }
      /* Shiny wraps selectInput in .form-group with a bottom margin; zeroing
         it lets align-items:flex-end line the controls up exactly. */
      .national-control-field .form-group {
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }
      /* The download occupies its own full-height column, set off by a rule
         so it reads as a separate action rather than a third control. */
      .national-control-action {
        flex: 0 0 auto;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        border-left: 1px solid #d8cdb8;
        padding-left: 1.5rem;
      }

      /* Download Selected Topic button */
      .btn-download-national {
        background: #013176 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #013176 !important;
        border-radius: 6px !important;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 1.1rem !important;
        font-weight: 700 !important;
        padding: 9px 20px !important;
        cursor: pointer !important;
        line-height: 1.4 !important;
        display: inline-flex !important;
        align-items: center !important;
        white-space: normal !important;
        text-align: left !important;
      }
      .btn-download-national:hover {
        background: #01214f !important;
        border-color: #01214f !important;
      }
      .btn-download-national:focus {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e !important;
        outline-offset: 2px !important;
        /* White halo in the offset gap so the ring does not rely on the page
           tone behind the button. White on #013176 is 12.34:1. */
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ffffff !important;
      }
      /* Narrow screens: stack the columns and turn the vertical rule into a
         horizontal one above the button. */
      @media (max-width: 900px) {
        .national-controls-split {
          flex-wrap: wrap;
        }
        .national-control-action {
          flex: 1 1 100%;
          justify-content: flex-start;
          border-left: none;
          border-top: 1px solid #d8cdb8;
          padding-left: 0;
          padding-top: 1rem;
        }
        .national-control-field .form-group {
          margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
        }
      }

      /* Length + search controls: left-aligned with some spacing */
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_length,
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_filter {
        float: left;
        text-align: left;
        margin-right: 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
      }
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_filter label {
        white-space: nowrap;
      }

      /* DT Buttons download button */
      .dt-buttons {
        float: left;
        margin-right: 1rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
      }
      .dt-button {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 1rem !important;
        font-weight: 600 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        background: #013176 !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #013176 !important;
        border-radius: 4px !important;
        padding: 4px 14px !important;
        cursor: pointer !important;
        line-height: 1.5 !important;
      }
      .dt-button:hover {
        background: #01214f !important;
        border-color: #01214f !important;
      }
      .dt-button:focus {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e !important;
        outline-offset: 2px !important;
      }

      /* ── National Data: card layout ───────────────────────────────────────── */

      /* Page header — warm beige background, maroon heading.
         Sized in px, not rem: this is a fluidPage(), so Bootstrap 3
         scaffolding sets `html { font-size: 10px }` and every rem here
         resolves against a 10px root. The old `1rem 1.5rem` padding was
         therefore 10px/15px and the `2.6rem` heading only 26px, which is
         why the band read as cramped. */
      .national-banner {
        background: #f9f7f4;
        border-bottom: 3px solid #e8e4db;
        padding: 20px 24px 18px;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0;
      }
      .national-banner h1 {
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 31px;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-bottom: 6px;
      }
      .national-banner .national-intro {
        color: #2c2c2c;
        margin-top: 0;
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }

      /* Base card */
      .national-card {
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-radius: 8px;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem 1.5rem 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(28, 43, 58, 0.07);
      }

      /* Maroon accent on top edge of each card */
      .national-controls-card,
      .national-map-card,
      .national-table-card {
        border-top: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
      }

      /* The map card carries more inside room than the other cards: the
         figure is the centrepiece of this tab and was sitting tight against
         the card edges. Paired with the taller girafe canvas below
         (height_svg 5 -> 6), which is what actually enlarges the map. */
      .national-map-card {
        padding: 18px 22px 26px 22px;
      }

      /* Topic summary band: its own space between the controls and the map.
         Kept lighter than the other cards (gold left rule, no maroon top bar,
         warm tint) so it reads as explanatory prose, not a fourth panel. */
      .national-summary-card {
        background: #fbf8f2;
        border: 1px solid #e6dcc6;
        border-left: 4px solid #c8a743;
        box-shadow: none;
        padding: 1.15rem 1.5rem;
      }
      /* Spans the full card width. The former `max-width: 78ch` capped the
         measure at roughly half the card and pushed the summary into a tall
         narrow column, leaving the right side of the band empty. The band is
         two or three sentences, so the taller-than-ideal measure costs less
         than the vertical space the cap was consuming. */
      .national-summary-card .map-summary {
        display: block;
        line-height: 1.55;
      }
      .national-summary-heading {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 19px;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.4rem 0;
        line-height: 1.3;
      }

      /* Sort arrow contrast: DataTables sets opacity:0.125 on ::before/::after;
         using table.dataTable.table_national gives higher specificity than
         DataTables own selectors so !important is not needed on most rules.
         Partial opacity was the reason the arrows read as grey: white at 0.6
         over the slate header resolves to a mid grey. Every arrow is now solid
         white at full opacity, and the active sort direction is picked out in
         gold so the sorted state is still obvious. */
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc {
        background-image: none !important;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting::after,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::after,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::after {
        opacity: 1 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        font-size: 14px !important;
        line-height: 11px !important;
        right: 9px !important;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::after {
        color: #f2c75c !important;   /* gold: active direction, 8.7:1 on slate */
      }
    "))
  ),

  tags$main(
    role = "main",

    # ── Page header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-banner",
      h1("National Data"),
      tags$p(
        class = "national-intro",
        "To explore the data first select a category and then a topic. You can navigate the boxes below using the mouse or keyboard."
      )
    ),

    # ── Controls card ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-controls-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "Data selection controls",
        # Single horizontal row: the two selectors on the left, the download on
        # the right behind a vertical rule. The topic summary is no longer part
        # of this card; it sits in its own card below. Stacks under 900px.
        div(
          class = "national-controls-split",
          div(
            class = "national-controls-row",
            div(
              class = "national-control-field",
              selectInput(
                inputId = "national_category_selector",
                label   = "Select a category",
                choices = c(
                  "Demographics",
                  "Community Living",
                  "Community Participation",
                  "Work/Economic"
                ),
                selected = "Demographics"
              )
            ),
            div(
              class = "national-control-field",
              selectInput(
                inputId  = "national_variable_selector",
                label    = "Select a topic",
                choices  = .initial_nat_choices,
                selected = .initial_nat_selected
              )
            )
          ),
          tags$section(
            `aria-label` = "Download the selected topic",
            class = "national-control-action",
            downloadButton(
              "download_national_topic",
              "Download Selected Topic",
              class        = "btn-download-national",
              icon         = dl_icon(),
              `aria-label` = "Download the selected topic as an accessible, print-ready ADA-PARC report: map and key on page one, full data table on page two"
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Topic summary card ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Given its own full-width band between the controls and the map so the
    # definition/high-low sentence reads as prose rather than as a caption
    # squeezed beside the controls.
    div(
      class = "national-card national-summary-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-labelledby` = "national-summary-heading",
        h2(
          "About This Topic",
          id    = "national-summary-heading",
          class = "national-summary-heading"
        ),
        div(
          `aria-live` = "polite",
          uiOutput("national_map_summary") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Map card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-map-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "Selected topic title",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_map_title") %>% withSpinner()
      ),
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "How to read the map",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_map_note")
      ),
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "State-by-state map of selected topic",
        div(
          id           = "national_map_img",
          role         = "img",
          `aria-label` = "Map of the United States. Use the topic dropdown to select a variable.",
          # Height tracks the girafe canvas aspect. opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE,
          # width = 1) scales the SVG to the container WIDTH and derives its
          # height from the width_svg:height_svg ratio, so this value only has
          # to be a container tall enough not to clip. At 10:6 a ~900px card
          # renders the figure about 540px tall.
          girafeOutput("national_ggmap", width = "100%", height = "560px") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # Tiny JS handler: updates the map div's aria-label reactively
    tags$script(HTML("
      Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('updateMapAriaLabel', function(x) {
        var el = document.getElementById('national_map_img');
        if (el) el.setAttribute('aria-label', x.label);
      });
    ")),

    # ── Table card ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-table-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "Data table for selected topic",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_table_title"),
        div(
          class = "table-container",
          uiOutput("national_table") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Source note ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    tags$section(
      `aria-label` = "Data source",
      `aria-live` = "polite",
      uiOutput("national_source_note")
    )
    # NOTE: the "Download Selected Topic" button previously lived here at the
    # foot of the page. It now sits in the controls card, to the right of the
    # category and topic selectors.
  )
  , adaparc_footer
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Flag to control rendering
  ready_to_render <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

  national_category_selected <- reactive({
    switch(
      input$national_category_selector %||% "Demographics",
      "Demographics"            = "is_demographics",
      "Community Participation" = "is_community_participation",
      "Community Living"        = "is_community_living",
      "Work/Economic"           = "is_work_economic"
    )
  })

  national_variable_choices <- reactive({
    tibble::deframe(
      dict_vars %>%
        filter(
          !!sym(national_category_selected()) == TRUE,
          !is.na(national_dropdown_label)
        ) %>%
        select(national_dropdown_label, var_readable)
    )
  })

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Pre-populate the topic selector BEFORE the first reactive flush so the
  # map + table render with defaults on initial page load (without the
  # user having to change a dropdown). Uses freezeReactiveValue so
  # downstream reactives don't see a transient NULL/"" during the
  # selectize rebuild.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  observe({
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "national_variable_selector")
    cat_col <- national_category_selected()
    init_choices <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(!!sym(cat_col) == TRUE, !is.na(national_dropdown_label)) %>%
      select(national_dropdown_label, var_readable) %>%
      tibble::deframe() %>%
      names()
    init_default <- if ("People with Disabilities" %in% init_choices) {
      "People with Disabilities"
    } else {
      init_choices[1]
    }
    updateSelectInput(
      session,
      "national_variable_selector",
      choices  = init_choices,
      selected = init_default
    )
  }, priority = 1000)

  # When both selectors have values, allow rendering
  observe({
    if (!is.null(input$national_category_selector) &&
        !is.null(input$national_variable_selector) &&
        nzchar(input$national_variable_selector)) {
      ready_to_render(TRUE)
    }
  })

  national_variable_selected <- reactive({
    req(national_category_selected())
    choices <- national_variable_choices()
    # If the select has not yet echoed its updated value back to the server,
    # fall back to the default so the table/map still render on first paint.
    current <- input$national_variable_selector
    if (is.null(current) || !nzchar(current) || !(current %in% names(choices))) {
      current <- if ("People with Disabilities" %in% names(choices)) {
        "People with Disabilities"
      } else {
        names(choices)[1]
      }
    }
    req(current)
    choices[[current]]
  })

  # Reactively update the map image's aria-label whenever the topic changes,
  # so screen readers announce which variable is currently shown on the map.
  #
  # AUDITED FOR THE STARTUP MESSAGE RACE. Phase 1.4 of
  # docs/palette-v2-build-plan.qmd, 2026-08-03. This observe() fires on the
  # session's first flush, so it sends during startup exactly as the display
  # panel's push did. It is NOT exposed to the same defect, for two independent
  # reasons, and both are properties of where the handler lives rather than
  # luck:
  #
  #   1. The handler is a tags$script in this app's own UI, a few lines below.
  #      It is registered while the browser parses the document body, which is
  #      finished before shiny.js opens the websocket, which is in turn before
  #      the server can flush anything back. Nothing can arrive first. The
  #      display panel's handler is in www/cssloaders.html, injected into the
  #      HEAD ahead of Shiny's own dependencies, so it runs at a point where
  #      `window.Shiny` may not exist yet and registration has to be deferred.
  #      That deferral is the race.
  #
  #   2. If a message were dropped anyway, the div carries a static aria-label
  #      in the markup and the next topic change re-sends. The failure would be
  #      a stale but valid label, not an unusable control.
  #
  # These are the only two sendCustomMessage call sites in this file. If a
  # third is added, and its handler is not in the same document's body, give it
  # a client-initiated handshake like display_panel_ready rather than trusting
  # the ordering.
  observe({
    req(national_variable_selected())
    topic_label <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()
    category_label <- input$national_category_selector
    new_label <- paste0(
      "Choropleth map of the United States showing ", topic_label,
      " (", category_label, ") by state.",
      " Use the topic dropdown above to change the variable displayed."
    )
    session$sendCustomMessage("updateMapAriaLabel", list(label = new_label))
  })

  # ── Shared topic bundle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single source of truth for the on-screen table AND the downloadable full
  # view. Building the friendly table, title, notes, and alt text here (rather
  # than separately in each output) guarantees the download always matches what
  # the user sees. Consumed by output$sortable_table and the download handler.
  national_topic_bundle <- reactive({
    req(ready_to_render())
    sel     <- national_variable_selected()
    req(sel)
    cat_col <- national_category_selected()

    var_row <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == sel) %>%
      head(1)

    title <- var_row %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    # Interpretation note: only for non-demographic, directional indicators.
    # Mirrors output$national_map_note so the download reads identically.
    is_demo <- isTRUE(var_row %>% pull(is_demographics))
    coding  <- var_row %>% pull(var_coding)
    interp_note <- ""
    if (!(is_demo || is.na(coding) || !(coding %in% c("pos", "neg")))) {
      # The colour reading holds for every series on these maps, not only the
      # disability series, so the note stays neutral on disability status.
      lead <- "Darker colors = more opportunity, lighter color = more disparity. "
      direction <- if (coding == "pos") {
        paste0("'", title, "' is a 'positive' indicator, meaning higher values indicate more opportunity.")
      } else {
        paste0("'", title, "' is a 'negative' indicator, meaning higher values indicate less opportunity.")
      }
      interp_note <- paste0(lead, direction)
    }

    # Source note (mirrors output$national_source_note)
    source_text <- var_row %>% pull(data_source_label)
    if (length(source_text) == 0 || is.na(source_text) || !nzchar(trimws(source_text))) {
      source_text <- "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
    }

    # Friendly table (mirrors former inline logic in output$sortable_table)
    national_vars_in_topic <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(
        (!!sym(cat_col)) == TRUE,
        var_topic == (dict_vars %>%
                        filter(
                          (!!sym(cat_col)) == TRUE &
                            var_readable == sel
                        ) %>%
                        pull(var_topic)),
        display == TRUE
      ) %>%
      select(var_pretty, var_readable)

    table_df <- national_data %>%
      mutate("State" = NAME) %>%
      arrange(State != "United States", State) %>%
      select(any_of(c("State", national_vars_in_topic %>% pull(var_readable)))) %>%
      mutate(
        across(
          c(starts_with("pct_"), ends_with("_pct")),
          ~ scales::percent(.x, accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)
        ),
        across(
          where(is.numeric) & !starts_with("pct_") & !ends_with("_pct"),
          ~ scales::comma(.x, accuracy = 1)
        )
      ) %>%
      rename(!!!national_vars_in_topic %>% deframe())

    list(
      sel         = sel,
      title       = title,
      category    = input$national_category_selector %||% "",
      interp_note = interp_note,
      source_note = source_text,
      alt_text    = altText(national_data, sel),
      table_df    = table_df,
      vars        = national_vars_in_topic
    )
  })

  output$national_map_summary <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    HTML(
      sprintf(
        '<span class="map-summary">%s</span>',
        altText(national_data, national_variable_selected())
      )
    )
  })

  output$national_source_note <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    source_text <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(data_source_label)
    if (length(source_text) == 0 || is.na(source_text) || !nzchar(trimws(source_text))) {
      source_text <- "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
    }
    tags$p(
      class = "national-source-note",
      tags$strong("This indicator sourced from: "),
      source_text
    )
  })

  output$national_map_title <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    title <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()
    div(h2(title, class = "national-map-title"))
  })

  output$national_table_title <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    title <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    div(h2(title, class = "national-map-title"))
  })

  # Interpretation note shown in its own container ABOVE the map. The note
  # only applies to non-demographic indicators with an explicit pos/neg
  # direction. Coloring is now directional (dark = better outcome), so the
  # note explains that convention and names the indicator's direction.
  output$national_map_note <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    var_row <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1)

    is_demo <- isTRUE(var_row %>% pull(is_demographics))
    coding  <- var_row %>% pull(var_coding)

    title <- var_row %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    if (is_demo || is.na(coding) || !(coding %in% c("pos", "neg"))) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    # Kept identical to the download copy above: the colour reading applies to
    # every series on the map, regardless of disability status.
    lead <- "Darker colors = more opportunity, lighter color = more disparity. "
    direction <- if (coding == "pos") {
      paste0("'", title, "' is a 'positive' indicator, meaning higher values indicate more opportunity.")
    } else {
      paste0("'", title, "' is a 'negative' indicator, meaning higher values indicate less opportunity.")
    }

    div(
      class = "map-interpretation-note",
      tags$span(class = "map-interpretation-note-label", "Interpretation Note: "),
      paste0(lead, direction)
    )
  })

  output$national_ggmap <- renderGirafe({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    gg <- render_national_map(
      national_variable_selected(),
      access_map_palette_selected(),
      na_color = access_map_na_selected()
    )
    girafe(
      ggobj      = gg,
      # 10 x 6 rather than 10 x 5. The legend sits at the bottom in two rows,
      # so the map panel was about 10 x 3.8, far wider than the Albers US
      # outline needs; the map was height-constrained and left large empty
      # flanks either side. A taller canvas gives the panel back to the map
      # instead of the margins. Legend and tooltip type do not change size,
      # since the SVG is scaled to the container width, not its height.
      width_svg  = 10,
      height_svg = 6,
      options    = list(
        opts_tooltip(
          css = paste0(
            "background:#1c2b3a; color:white; ",
            "font-family:'EB Garamond',Georgia,serif; ",
            "font-size:15px; padding:8px 11px; border-radius:6px; ",
            "line-height:1.55; white-space:pre;"
          ),
          offx = 12, offy = -28, use_cursor_pos = TRUE
        ),
        # Deliberately sets stroke-WIDTH only, never stroke colour. Each state
        # now carries a border colour chosen from its own fill (near-black on
        # the light half of the ramp, white on the dark half; see the State
        # border ink notes in scripts/functions.R). Forcing a single navy on
        # hover, as this did before, overwrote that and left dark-filled states
        # with a 1.3:1 hover outline they could not show. Widening the state's
        # own ink keeps the hover affordance legible on every bin and in every
        # palette.
        opts_hover(css = "fill-opacity:0.75; stroke-width:2px;"),
        opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE, width = 1),
        opts_toolbar(saveaspng = FALSE),
        opts_selection(type = "none")
      )
    )
  })

  output$national_table <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    DT::dataTableOutput("sortable_table", width = "100%")
  })

  output$sortable_table <- DT::renderDataTable({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    # Table content comes from the shared bundle so it always matches the
    # downloadable full view (see national_topic_bundle above).
    bundle <- national_topic_bundle()
    national_data_table_friendly <- bundle$table_df

    all_columns      <- colnames(national_data_table_friendly)
    sortable_columns <- which(grepl("State|%", all_columns))

    # DataTables uses 0-based column indices; 0 is the State column
    non_state_columns <- setdiff(seq_along(all_columns) - 1, 0)

    # Per-table CSV export removed: downloading is now handled by the single
    # "Download Selected Topic" full-view button at the bottom of the page.
    DT::datatable(
      national_data_table_friendly,
      options = list(
        pageLength = -1,  # show all rows by default
        lengthMenu = list(
          c(10, 25, 50, -1),
          c("10", "25", "50", "All")
        ),
        scrollX   = TRUE,
        autoWidth = FALSE,
        columnDefs = list(
          # Make some columns unsortable
          list(
            targets   = setdiff(seq_along(all_columns) - 1, sortable_columns - 1),
            orderable = FALSE
          ),
          # Right-align all non-State columns
          list(
            targets   = non_state_columns,
            className = 'dt-right'
          )
        ),
        dom     = "lfrtip"  # length, filter, table, info, paging (no Buttons)
      ),
      rownames = FALSE,
      width    = "100%",
      # "compact" dropped: its 4px cell padding fought the roomier row
      # heights set in the national table CSS above.
      class    = "display table_national"
    )
  }, server = FALSE)

  # ── Download Selected Topic: full branded HTML view ─────────────────────────
  # Renders national_topic.qmd for the current selection into a self-contained,
  # ADA-PARC branded HTML: page 1 (banner, title, map + key, notes), page 2
  # (data table). All content is prepared here and passed via an RDS bundle so
  # the download always matches the on-screen view.
  nd_app_root <- normalizePath(
    getOption("shiny.appdir", default = getwd()),
    mustWork = FALSE
  )
  national_dir  <- file.path(nd_app_root, "national")
  national_qmd  <- file.path(national_dir, "national_topic.qmd")
  nd_out_dir    <- file.path(tempdir(), "ada_parc_national_dl")
  dir.create(nd_out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  output$download_national_topic <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
      bundle <- national_topic_bundle()
      slug   <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", bundle$title)
      slug   <- gsub("^_|_$", "", slug)
      paste0("ADA-PARC_", slug, "_2024.html")
    },
    content = function(file) {
      withProgress(
        message = "Building your ADA-PARC report…",
        detail  = "This usually takes 15–25 seconds.",
        value   = 0.2,
        {
          bundle <- national_topic_bundle()

          # Render the map (ggplot from render_national_map) to an inline SVG
          # string. svglite emits the requested font-family; the browser pairs
          # it with the EB Garamond webfont loaded via font-loader.html.
          gg <- render_national_map(
            bundle$sel,
            access_map_palette_selected(),
            na_color = access_map_na_selected()
          )
          svg_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
          ggplot2::ggsave(
            filename = svg_tmp, plot = gg,
            device = svglite::svglite,
            width = 9, height = 6.4, bg = "white"
          )
          map_svg <- paste(readLines(svg_tmp, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
          unlink(svg_tmp)

          setProgress(0.45, detail = "Composing the document…")

          out_bundle <- list(
            title       = bundle$title,
            category    = bundle$category,
            interp_note = bundle$interp_note,
            source_note = bundle$source_note,
            alt_text    = bundle$alt_text,
            table_df    = bundle$table_df,
            map_svg     = map_svg,
            generated   = format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")
          )
          bundle_path <- file.path(nd_out_dir, "bundle.rds")
          saveRDS(out_bundle, bundle_path)

          setProgress(0.6, detail = "Rendering HTML…")

          tryCatch({
            quarto::quarto_render(
              input          = national_qmd,
              execute_params = list(bundle = bundle_path),
              execute_dir    = national_dir
            )
            rendered <- file.path(national_dir, "national_topic.html")
            if (file.exists(rendered)) {
              file.copy(rendered, file, overwrite = TRUE)
            } else {
              writeLines("<html><body>Report could not be generated.</body></html>", file)
            }
            setProgress(1)
          }, error = function(e) {
            showNotification(
              ui       = paste("Download failed:", conditionMessage(e)),
              type     = "error",
              duration = 15
            )
            writeLines(
              paste0("<html><body>Report could not be generated: ",
                     htmltools::htmlEscape(conditionMessage(e)), "</body></html>"),
              file
            )
          })
        }
      )
    }
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

# City Data

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(leaflet.extras2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(shinycssloaders)

# ----------------------------
# State choices
# ----------------------------
state_choices <- tibble::tibble(NAME = state.name, ABB = state.abb) %>%
  add_row(NAME = c("District of Columbia", "Puerto Rico"), ABB = c("DC", "PR")) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

# ----------------------------
# Helpers (ALL pct cols are dbl on 0–100 scale)
# ----------------------------
fmt_pct_1dp <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.1))
}

# As above, but adds precision as the value shrinks: one decimal at 1% and
# above, two decimals under 1%, three decimals under 0.01%. One decimal
# alone rounds small shares to 0.0% and loses them; two decimals still
# rounds the smallest shares (well under 0.01%) to 0.00%. Used on the
# Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age demographics list, where "share of total
# population" figures routinely fall under 1%.
fmt_pct_dynamic <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA",
         ifelse(abs(x) < 0.01,
                scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.001),
                ifelse(abs(x) < 1,
                       scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.01),
                       scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.1))))
}

fmt_num <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", scales::comma(x, accuracy = 1))
}

create_number_percent_string <- function(num, pct) {
  paste0(fmt_num(num), " (", fmt_pct_1dp(pct), ")")
}

# Dollar formatter for ACS median earnings (B18140).
#
# ACS reports a median that falls in the top or bottom interval as the
# bound itself, so the raw values 250001 and 2499 are not real medians and
# must not be printed as though they were. Across the 8,407 places, 6 are
# top-coded and 40 are bottom-coded.
fmt_dollar <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x)    ~ "Not available",
    x >= 250001 ~ "$250,000 or more",
    x <= 2499   ~ "$2,500 or less",
    TRUE        ~ scales::dollar(x, accuracy = 1)
  )
}

# As above, but collapses to a plain-language phrase when the percentage is
# suppressed, so the reader sees "Not available" rather than "NA (NA)".
# Used for indicators that are genuinely missing for some places: health
# insurance (a handful of places) and anything sourced from ACS S1811,
# which resolves for only 694 of 8,407 places.
create_number_percent_string_or_na <- function(num, pct) {
  ifelse(is.na(as.numeric(pct)), "Not available",
         paste0(fmt_num(num), " (", fmt_pct_1dp(pct), ")"))
}

# As fmt_pct_1dp, but "Not available" rather than "NA" for a missing value.
# Used where there is no paired count to fall back on the way
# create_number_percent_string_or_na does: HUD housing access is a rate
# with no numerator/denominator pair carried on this page.
fmt_pct_or_na <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "Not available", fmt_pct_1dp(x))
}

# One decimal place, "mi" suffix, "Not available" for a missing value. Used
# for the Centers for Independent Living distance measures, which are place-
# level straight-line distances rather than a rate with a numerator/
# denominator pair.
fmt_miles_or_na <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "Not available", paste0(scales::comma(x, accuracy = 0.1), " mi"))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paired with/without-disability comparison tables (City Data tab)
#
# Every outcome indicator on the city page has a without-disability
# counterpart in city_place_full.Rds, at equal or better coverage. These two
# helpers render a pair as an accessible two-column table rather than as a
# bullet list, because a bullet carrying two values reads as a run-on
# sentence and gives screen reader users no column context.
#
# The PWD-to-PWOD column pairs MUST be declared explicitly. The naming is not
# consistent and cannot be derived: unemployment is
# pct_cni_18to64_nodis_unemployed, with "nodis" before the measure, while its
# neighbour is pct_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis with "nodis" after, and the
# health insurance columns put "nodis" in the middle. A
# paste0(var, "_nodis") would fail silently on several of them.
#
# cmp_row() builds one row spec. kind = "count_pct" formats as
# "12,345 (12.3%)"; kind = "dollar" formats a single ACS median with the
# top-code and bottom-code guards in fmt_dollar().
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cmp_row <- function(label, dis, nodis, kind = "count_pct", dis_pop = NA_character_,
                    nodis_pop = NA_character_) {
  list(label = label, dis = dis, nodis = nodis, kind = kind,
       dis_pop = dis_pop, nodis_pop = nodis_pop)
}

render_comparison_table <- function(row, rows, caption) {
  cell <- function(pct_col, pop_col, kind) {
    if (identical(kind, "dollar")) {
      fmt_dollar(row[[pct_col]])
    } else {
      create_number_percent_string_or_na(row[[pop_col]], row[[pct_col]])
    }
  }

  body <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    paste0(
      "<tr><th scope=\"row\">", r$label, "</th>",
      "<td>", cell(r$dis,   r$dis_pop,   r$kind), "</td>",
      "<td>", cell(r$nodis, r$nodis_pop, r$kind), "</td></tr>"
    )
  }, character(1))

  paste0(
    "<table class=\"city-compare\">",
    "<caption>", caption, "</caption>",
    "<thead><tr>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">Indicator</th>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">With disability</th>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">Without disability</th>",
    "</tr></thead><tbody>",
    paste0(body, collapse = ""),
    "</tbody></table>"
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Disability Demographics list (Race/Ethnicity, Sex, Age) on the City Data tab
#
# Simplified per Colin's client's request 2026-08-18: these three groups
# used to render as four-column tables (see git history / render_share_table()
# for the prior version), answering three separate questions per group
# (disability rate within the group, share of the city's PWD, share of the
# total population). The client asked to drop back to a single, plainly
# readable figure per group:
#   - the number of people in that group with a disability
#     -> pop_cni_<group>_dis
#   - that number's share of the city's total population
#     -> pop_cni_<group>_dis / pop_cni_total_all
#     ("Of everyone in this city, what share is both disabled and X?")
#
# Both are derivable from columns already present in city_place(): the
# disabled headcount per group (pop_cni_<group>_dis) and the city's total
# population (pop_cni_total_all). No new pipeline variables are needed.
# Renders as a plain <ul>, not a table, per the client's request for a
# cleaner, simpler look; a native list still gives screen reader users list
# structure without table markup the two figures no longer need.
#
# Layout, 2026-08-18 second follow-up: each group is a stat tile rather than
# a single label/value line, and the <ul> is a responsive CSS grid, so the
# groups fill the full-width card instead of stacking in one narrow column
# that left most of the card empty. Inside a tile the reading order is
# label, then the share of total population set large as the headline
# figure, then the count on its own line. Sizing and colour live in the
# stylesheet (.city-demo-list and friends); this function only emits markup.
#
# Accessibility notes on the tile markup:
#   - the <ul>/<li> structure is unchanged, so screen readers still announce
#     the group count and step through one group at a time;
#   - the headline percentage is visually labelled only by its position, so
#     a visually hidden span (.city-demo-sr) carries the words a sighted
#     reader gets from the heading above and the count below. Without it the
#     percentage would be read as a bare number;
#   - nothing is encoded in colour, and the count is text, not a bar.
#
# The whole figure block is built in one is.na() branch rather than
# concatenated from separately-computed pieces, so a missing group_dis
# collapses cleanly to a single "Not available" tile rather than pairing a
# real "Not available" with a leftover formatted "NA".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
demo_row <- function(label, group_dis_pop) {
  list(label = label, group_dis_pop = group_dis_pop)
}

# One tile. Split out of render_demo_list() on 2026-08-18 so the Disability
# Types block can emit the same markup without duplicating the class names
# in a second place. label and figure are both already-built HTML.
demo_tile <- function(label, figure) {
  paste0(
    "<li class=\"city-demo-tile\">",
    "<span class=\"city-demo-label\">", label, "</span>",
    figure,
    "</li>"
  )
}

# The figure half of a tile: headline percentage, then the count beneath it.
# Both the demographics groups and the disability types express the same
# quantity, a share of the city's total population, so both carry the same
# visually hidden wording. Built in one branch rather than concatenated from
# separately-computed pieces, so a missing value collapses to a single
# "Not available" rather than pairing a real "Not available" with a
# leftover formatted "NA".
demo_figure <- function(pct, count) {
  pct   <- as.numeric(pct)
  count <- as.numeric(count)
  if (is.na(pct)) {
    return("<span class=\"city-demo-na\">Not available</span>")
  }
  paste0(
    "<span class=\"city-demo-pct\">",
    fmt_pct_dynamic(pct),
    "<span class=\"city-demo-sr\"> of the city's total population</span>",
    "</span>",
    if (is.na(count)) {
      ""
    } else {
      paste0("<span class=\"city-demo-count\">", fmt_num(count), " people</span>")
    }
  )
}

# note is optional explanatory prose shown between the heading and the tiles.
# Added 2026-08-18 for the Age block, whose under-5 caveat previously sat
# above the "Age" heading, where it read as though it applied to Sex. It
# carries .city-summary-help, the on-screen note class, which the download
# template also styles (see .tbl-block p.city-summary-help in
# city/city_profile.qmd), so the one fragment reads correctly in both.
render_demo_list <- function(row, rows, heading, note = NULL) {
  total_pop <- as.numeric(row$pop_cni_total_all)

  items <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    group_dis <- as.numeric(row[[r$group_dis_pop]])
    pct <- if (is.na(group_dis) || is.na(total_pop) || total_pop == 0) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      100 * group_dis / total_pop
    }
    demo_tile(r$label, demo_figure(pct, group_dis))
  }, character(1))

  paste0(
    "<p class=\"city-demo-heading\">", heading, "</p>",
    if (is.null(note) || !nzchar(note)) {
      ""
    } else {
      paste0("<p class=\"city-summary-help\">", note, "</p>")
    },
    "<ul class=\"city-demo-list\">",
    paste0(items, collapse = ""),
    "</ul>"
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Disability Types tiles
#
# Same tile aesthetic as the demographics lists, per Colin's 2026-08-18
# request. Previously a plain <ul> of "Hearing - 12,345 (2.3%)" bullets.
#
# The percentages here come straight from the pipeline's pct_cni_* columns
# rather than being derived from a count and a denominator, because these
# are already shares of the city's total population (see
# help$disability_types_intro), which is exactly what the demographics
# tiles show. So the two blocks are directly comparable and the same
# visually hidden wording inside .city-demo-pct is correct for both.
#
# No wrapping <ul> is added by the caller: this returns the complete list,
# unlike the earlier bullets fragment.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
type_row <- function(label, count_col, pct_col) {
  list(label = label, count_col = count_col, pct_col = pct_col)
}

render_type_list <- function(row, rows) {
  items <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    demo_tile(r$label, demo_figure(row[[r$pct_col]], row[[r$count_col]]))
  }, character(1))

  paste0(
    "<ul class=\"city-demo-list\">",
    paste0(items, collapse = ""),
    "</ul>"
  )
}

# Join-proof tract GEOID normalization (NO percent conversion)
normalize_tract_geoid <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", x)                   # digits only
  ifelse(nchar(x) >= 11, substr(x, nchar(x) - 10, nchar(x)), x)  # last 11 digits
}

# ----------------------------
# UI

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* ── City Data tab: font + design tokens ──────────────────────────── */
      /* @import here because the shinyApp sub-context does not reliably     */
      /* inherit www/styles.css from the parent flexdashboard.               */
      @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=EB+Garamond:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;0,800;1,400&display=swap');

      /* Universal font rule — covers Bootstrap resets and dynamic widgets */
      *, *::before, *::after {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
      }

      body {
        background: #f9f7f4;
      }

      /* Page header banner */
      /* Banner geometry, title and intro line are kept byte-for-byte identical
         to .national-banner / .national-banner h1 / .national-intro so the two
         tabs open with the same header block. Values are in px because
         Bootstrap 3 sets html{font-size:10px}, which makes rem units render
         ~62% of their intended size here. */
      .city-banner {
        background: #f9f7f4;
        border-bottom: 3px solid #e8e4db;
        padding: 20px 24px 18px;

         this header line. */
      .city-banner .city-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        font-weight: 400;
        line-height: inherit;

      }

      .city-note-footer {

      /* Section cards */

      /* ── Controls row + download action ────────────────────────────────
         Mirrors .national-controls-split / .national-control-action in the
         National Data tab: selectors on the left, the download behind a
         full-height rule on the right, so the two tabs' controls read the
         same way. */
      .city-controls-split {

      }
      .city-summary h3,
      .city-summary h4,
      .city-summary p,
      .city-summary ul,
      .city-summary li,
      .city-summary b {
        color: #1c1c1c;
      }
      .city-summary h3 {
        font-size: 2.4rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin: 0.25rem 0 0.9rem 0;
        padding-bottom: 0.45rem;

        color: #1c2b3a;
        letter-spacing: -0.01em;
      }

        font-size: 2rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-top: 1.4rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;

        font-weight: 700;
      }
      /* Sub-headings inside a summary card: Health Insurance, Education,
         Employment, and so on. Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age carry their own
         heading style, .city-demo-heading, styled below near .city-demo-list.
         The two descendant selectors below were written for an older
         markup where the b element sat inside a nested div; in the
         current markup the b element is a direct child of .city-summary,
         so neither matched and sub-headings were rendering at inherited
         body size, smaller than the 1.5rem list items they label. The
         direct-child selector is the one that actually applies. The other
         two are kept in case that markup returns. */
      .city-summary > b,
      .city-summary > div > b,
      .city-summary .col-md-12 > b {
        display: inline-block;
        font-size: 1.55rem;
        font-weight: 700;

      }

      }

      }

      /* Paired with/without-disability comparison tables.
         Semantic tables rather than bullet lists: column and row headers are
         announced by screen readers, and tabular figures keep the two value
         columns aligned so the comparison is readable at a glance. */
      .city-summary table.city-compare {
        width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse;
        margin: 0.35rem 0 1.1rem;
        font-size: 1.4rem;
        line-height: 1.5;
```
