```{r}
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare th,
      .city-summary table.city-compare td {
        border: 1px solid #ded8cf;
        padding: 0.4rem 0.55rem;
        text-align: left;
        vertical-align: top;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare thead th {
        background: #1c2b3a;
        color: #ffffff;
        font-weight: 600;
        border-color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 1.3rem;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] {
        background: #f6f2ec;
        font-weight: 600;
        width: 42%;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare tbody tr:nth-child(even) td {
        background: #fbf9f6;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare td {
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      /* Narrow screens: allow the value columns to wrap rather than forcing a
         horizontal scroll inside the card. */
      @media (max-width: 62em) {
        .city-summary table.city-compare td { white-space: normal; }
        .city-summary table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] { width: 38%; }
      }

      /* Full-width outcome cards (Community Participation, Work and
         Economic), stacked one above the other since 2026-08-18 rather than
         sharing a row as col-md-6 halves. With twice the width available,
         the type inside them goes up rather than the tables simply getting
         wider: at half width these tables were set at 1.4rem to fit, which
         is the smallest text on the card and sits below the 1.5rem list
         items beside it. The sizes below bring the tables level with the
         rest of the card and give the cells room to breathe.

         Gated on min-width 62em, Bootstrap 3's md breakpoint and the point
         at which these cards would previously have split into halves.
         Below it the card is full width for every layout anyway and the
         compact sizes above, including the narrow-screen th width in the
         media query directly above this one, still apply. Selectors carry
         both class names so they outrank the base .city-summary rules on
         specificity rather than on source order alone. */
      @media (min-width: 62em) {
        /* max-width, not width, so the table still fills a narrower card.
           On a wide monitor a 100%-width three-column table pushes the two
           value columns so far apart that the eye loses the row it is
           reading; the cap holds the comparison within one comfortable
           glance, the same measure the downloadable report gets from its
           8.5in page. Well above the point where the columns would crowd. */
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare {
          font-size: 1.6rem;
          line-height: 1.55;
          margin: 0.45rem 0 1.4rem;
          max-width: 110rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare caption {
          font-size: 1.7rem;
          padding-bottom: 0.4rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare th,
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare td {
          padding: 0.6rem 0.85rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare thead th {
          font-size: 1.5rem;
        }
        /* The label column no longer needs 42% of a half-width card; at full
           width that would strand the two value columns far to the right of
           the text they belong to. */
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] {
          width: 34%;
        }
        /* Sub-headings (Health Insurance, Employment, ...) and their notes,
           raised to keep the same step down from heading to note to table
           that the card had at the smaller sizes. */
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack > b {
          font-size: 1.75rem;
          margin-top: 1.1rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack .city-summary-help {
          font-size: 1.5rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack ul {
          font-size: 1.6rem;
        }
      }

      /* Disability Demographics stat tiles (Race/Ethnicity, Sex, Age).
         Simplified per Colin's client's request 2026-08-18: these three
         groups no longer render as four-column tables (count, rate within
         group, share of city PWD, share of total population). Each group
         now shows two figures, its share of the city's total population as
         the headline and the count beneath it. See render_demo_list().

         Laid out as a responsive grid of tiles, replacing the earlier
         single narrow column. That column was capped at 30rem to keep a
         short label near its value, which fixed the gap but left most of
         this full-width card (.city-summary-wide) empty and made the eight
         race groups read as one undifferentiated stack. auto-fill rather
         than auto-fit is deliberate: with auto-fit a two-item list, Sex,
         would stretch its two tiles across the entire card, so the tile
         size would change from section to section. auto-fill holds the
         track width steady and simply leaves the unused tracks empty.

         Still a native ul/li, so screen readers announce the group count
         and step through one group at a time. The visually hidden span
         inside the percentage (.city-demo-sr) supplies the wording a
         sighted reader takes from the tile layout; without it the headline
         reads as a bare number. Nothing is carried by colour alone. */
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list {
        list-style: none;
        margin: 0.35rem 0 1.2rem 0;
        padding: 0;
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(24rem, 1fr));
        gap: 0.9rem;
      }
      /* Two tiles across, fixed, inside the full-width summary card.
         Changed from the auto-fill tracks above on 2026-08-18: at a desktop
         width auto-fill gave four or five tiles per row, which spread the
         eight race groups and the six disability types into a wide, dense
         band under the map. Two fixed columns run the same content down the
         page instead, closer to the downloadable report's shape, and give
         each tile enough width that no label wraps past two lines.
         The auto-fill rule above still applies to any city-demo-list that
         appears outside this card. */
      .city-summary-wide ul.city-demo-list {
        grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
      }
      /* Below roughly a tablet width two tiles are narrower than the long
         race labels want, so drop to one. */
      @media (max-width: 48em) {
        .city-summary-wide ul.city-demo-list {
          grid-template-columns: 1fr;
        }
      }
      /* At two columns in a full-width card each tile is wide enough that
         even the longest label (Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander,
         Ambulatory (difficulty walking or climbing stairs)) stays on one
         line, so the two-line floor below would leave a visible empty band
         above every percentage. Dropped to a one-line floor here only. The
         3.9rem floor still applies between 48em and 62em, where two columns
         are narrow enough that labels do wrap and the percentages need it
         to stay level across a row. */
      @media (min-width: 62em) {
        .city-summary-wide ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-label {
          min-height: 2rem;
        }
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list li.city-demo-tile {
        background: #faf8f5;
        border: 1px solid #e0dbd2;
        border-left: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
        border-radius: 4px;
        padding: 0.9rem 1.1rem 1rem 1.1rem;
        margin: 0;
      }
      /* min-height reserves two lines for the label so the headline
         percentages line up across a row of tiles even when one label
         wraps (Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander is the long one).
         It is a floor, not a cap, so a third line still fits on narrow
         screens. */
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-label {
        display: block;
        font-size: 1.45rem;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.35;
        min-height: 3.9rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.35rem;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-pct {
        display: block;
        font-size: 2.8rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        line-height: 1.1;
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-count {
        display: block;
        font-size: 1.4rem;
        color: #3a3a3a;
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
        margin-top: 0.15rem;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-na {
        display: block;
        font-size: 1.6rem;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #3a3a3a;
      }
      /* Visually hidden, but still read aloud and still found by in-page
         search on most browsers. Standard clip pattern rather than
         display:none, which would remove it from the accessibility tree
         and defeat the purpose. */
      .city-summary .city-demo-sr {
        position: absolute;
        width: 1px;
        height: 1px;
        padding: 0;
        margin: -1px;
        overflow: hidden;
        clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
        clip-path: inset(50%);
        white-space: nowrap;
        border: 0;
      }
      /* Sub-heading above each list (Race / Ethnicity, Sex, Age). Reuses
         the same visual weight as the other <b> sub-headings on this card
         (Employment, Earnings, ...) so the demographics card matches the
         rest of the page now that it no longer relies on a table caption
         for this label. */
      /* Enlarged 1.55rem -> 1.85rem on 2026-08-18. At the old size these
         three labels sat level with the body copy around them and did not
         read as the section breaks they are. 1.85rem keeps them clearly
         below the 2rem h4 above them (Disability Demographics) while
         sitting well above the 1.5rem tile labels below. */
      .city-summary p.city-demo-heading {
        font-size: 1.85rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        letter-spacing: 0.01em;
        margin: 1.4rem 0 0.45rem 0;
      }
      /* The Age note now sits between the Age heading and its tiles, so it
         needs to hug the heading rather than carry the standalone
         paragraph spacing .city-summary-help uses elsewhere. */
      .city-summary p.city-demo-heading + p.city-summary-help {
        margin-top: 0.2rem;
      }
      /* With the card-level h3 headings removed, the first sub-section
         heading sits flush at the top of each card rather than carrying
         the inter-section spacing meant to separate blocks. */
      .city-summary h4:first-child {
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
      }

      /* An equal-height .city-summary-row rule used to live here, making the
         two side-by-side outcome cards flex items so the shorter one did not
         leave a ragged edge. Removed 2026-08-18 along with the col-md-6
         halves themselves: every outcome card is full width now, so no two
         cards ever sit beside each other. */

      /* Full-width demographics card (row two).
         Holds both Disability Demographics and Disability Types. Everything
         inside stacks in a single vertical column at every width. An earlier
         version flowed the longer lists into two CSS columns to use the extra
         width, but two columns of bullets read worse than one, so the lists
         run straight down and the card simply ends where its content ends. */

      /* Full-width explanatory card, used for the Community Living domain,
         which has no city-level indicators available yet. Lighter treatment
         than a data card so it does not read as though data is missing. */
      .city-summary-note {
        background: #faf8f5;
        border-top-width: 3px;
      }
      .city-summary-note h4:first-child {
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
      }

      /* Shared heading above both summary columns. Mirrors .city-summary
         h3 and p, but sits outside the cards so it can span the full
         width and centre over the two-column layout below it. */
      .city-summary-header {
        text-align: center;
        margin: 1.25rem 0 0 0;
        padding: 0 0.5rem;
      }
      .city-summary-header h3 {
        font-size: 2.4rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin: 0.25rem 0 0.9rem 0;
        padding-bottom: 0.45rem;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #1c2b3a;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        letter-spacing: -0.01em;
      }
      .city-summary-header p {
        font-size: 1.55rem;
        line-height: 1.75;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        margin: 0 auto;
        max-width: 90ch;
      }

      /* ── Select inputs: font, sizing, and maroon accent on focus ──────── */
      .control-label {
        font-size: 20px !important;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.3rem;
      }
      .selectize-input,
      .selectize-dropdown,
      .selectize-dropdown-content,
      .selectize-input input,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .active {
        font-size: 19px !important;
      }
      .selectize-input {
        border: 1.5px solid #5c6672 !important;
        border-radius: 4px !important;
        background: #fff !important;
        color: #1c1c1c !important;
        padding: 7px 10px !important;
      }
      .selectize-input.focus,
      .selectize-input:focus-within {
        border-color: #0d3b8e !important;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(13, 59, 142, 0.15) !important;
        outline: none !important;
      }
      .selectize-dropdown {
        border: 1.5px solid #5c6672 !important;
        border-top: none !important;
        border-radius: 0 0 4px 4px !important;
        background: #fff !important;
      }
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option:hover,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option.active,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .selected {
        background: #013176 !important;
        color: #fff !important;
      }

      /* ── Leaflet legend ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
      /* Sized in px, not rem: Bootstrap 3 scaffolding sets html font-size to
         10px, so a rem value here renders ~62% of its intended size. The key
         previously read 1.1rem and came out at 11px. */
      .leaflet-container .legend {
        font-size: 17px !important;
        line-height: 1.45 !important;
        color: #1c1c1c !important;
        background: rgba(255,255,255,1.0) !important;
        padding: 12px 16px !important;
        border-radius: 6px !important;
        box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.18);
      }
      .leaflet-container .legend .info {
        background: transparent !important;
      }
      /* Legend title sits in a leading div > strong */
      .leaflet-container .legend div strong {
        font-size: 18px !important;
        font-weight: 700 !important;
        display: inline-block;
        margin-bottom: 4px;
      }
      /* Colour swatches: leaflet's inline defaults are 18px squares; scale
         them with the larger text so the key stays legible. The black
         outline keeps the palest bin and the white-ish no-data swatch
         distinguishable from the legend background. */
      .leaflet-container .legend i {
        width: 22px !important;
        height: 22px !important;
        margin-right: 8px !important;
        border: 1px solid #000 !important;
        box-sizing: border-box !important;
      }

      /* Focus ring: maroon to match new palette */
      :focus-visible {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e !important;
        outline-offset: 2px;
      }
    "))
  ),

  tags$main(
    role = "main",

    # ── Page header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-banner",
      tags$h1("City Data", class = "city-title"),
      tags$p(
        class = "city-note",
        "Select a state and city to explore tract-level disability data and community statistics."
      )
    ),

    # ── Controls card ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-card city-controls-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "City selection controls",
        div(
          class = "city-controls-split",
          div(
            class = "city-controls-row",
            div(
              class = "city-control-field",
              selectInput(
                "state_selector", "Select a state",
                choices = names(state_choices),
                selected = "Illinois"
              )
            ),
            div(class = "city-control-field", uiOutput("city_selector_ui"))
          ),
          tags$section(
            `aria-label` = "Download the selected city",
            class = "city-control-action",
            downloadButton(
              "download_city",
              "Download Selected City",
              class        = "btn-download-city",
              icon         = dl_icon(),
              `aria-label` = "Download the selected city as an accessible, print-ready ADA-PARC report: map and key, then summary tables for people with disabilities in this city"
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Map card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-card city-map-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "City tract map showing disability rates",
        fluidRow(
          column(12, div(`aria-live` = "polite", withSpinner(uiOutput("city_map_title")))),
          column(12, withSpinner(leafletOutput("snapshotmap", height = 550)))
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Summary card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-card city-data-summary-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "City summary statistics for people with disabilities",
        fluidRow(
          column(12, div(`aria-live` = "polite", withSpinner(uiOutput("city_summary"))))
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Footer note ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    tags$p(
      class = "city-note city-note-footer",
      # Coverage wording corrected 31 July 2026. The previous text attributed
      # missing values to a population threshold of 30,000, which is wrong:
      # 1,322 selectable cities exceed that population but only 648 carry the
      # education and commuting measures. The Census rule keys on the size of
      # the population with disabilities, with the cutoff falling between
      # 7,178 and 7,883 residents across the 8,407 places in the file.
      "Note: Some measures are not published for every city. The Census releases the education and commuting figures only where the population with disabilities is large enough, roughly 7,500 residents, so those two sections are shown for 648 of the cities in this tool and hidden for the rest. Other Not Applicable or NA values may appear where a figure was suppressed for that city. Percentages built on a small population count, such as a race or ethnicity group of only a few dozen residents in a given city, can shift dramatically based on a handful of survey responses and carry a wide margin of error, so treat figures drawn from small subgroups with caution."
    )
  )
  , adaparc_footer
)

# ----------------------------
# Server
# ----------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  # --- State selection ---
  state_selected <- reactive({
    req(input$state_selector)
    state_abbr <- state_choices[[input$state_selector]]
    req(!is.null(state_abbr))
    state_abbr
  })

  # --- City choices for selected state ---
  city_choices <- reactive({
    req(state_selected())
    choices <- dict_location_crosswalk %>%
      filter(state == state_selected(), !str_detect(place_NAME, " CDP")) %>%
      select(place_NAME, place_GEOID) %>%
      distinct(place_NAME, place_GEOID)
    req(nrow(choices) > 0)
    tibble::deframe(choices) %>% sort()
  })

  output$city_selector_ui <- renderUI({
    selectInput("city_selector", "Select a city",
                choices = names(city_choices()),
                selected = "Chicago")
  })

  observeEvent(input$state_selector, {
    updateSelectInput(session, "city_selector",
                      choices = names(city_choices()),
                      selected = "Chicago")
  })

  # --- City selected GEOID ---
  city_selected <- reactive({
    req(input$city_selector, city_choices())
    selected_city <- city_choices()[input$city_selector]
    req(!is.null(selected_city))
    selected_city
  })

  # --- Place-level data for the selected city ---
  city_place <- reactive({
    req(city_selected())
    city_data <- city_place_full %>% filter(GEOID == city_selected())
    req(nrow(city_data) > 0)
    city_data
  })

  # --- Tract SF and tract data for selected city ---
  city_tract_sf <- reactive({
    req(city_selected())
    tract_ids <- dict_location_crosswalk %>%
      filter(place_GEOID %in% city_selected()) %>%
      pull(tract_GEOID)
    req(length(tract_ids) > 0)
    tracts_sf %>% filter(tract_GEOID %in% tract_ids)
  })

  city_tract <- reactive({
    req(city_selected())
    tract_ids <- dict_location_crosswalk %>%
      filter(place_GEOID %in% city_selected()) %>%
      pull(tract_GEOID)
    req(length(tract_ids) > 0)
    tracts_data %>% filter(GEOID %in% tract_ids)
  })

  # --- City map title ---
  output$city_map_title <- renderUI({
    req(city_place())
    title <- city_place() %>%
      mutate(NAME = str_replace_all(NAME, " (city|village|municipality|town), ", ", ")) %>%
      pull(NAME)
    div(h4(title, class = "city-map-title"))
  })

  # ----------------------------
  # MAP: fixed national classification + leaflet render
  #
  # Place these EXACTLY here: after city_tract()/city_tract_sf() reactives exist,
  # and before output$city_summary.
  #
  # city_map_breaks / city_map_labels are FIXED (computed once at app start
  # from the full national tract distribution -- see setup chunk). Only the
  # 4 discrete colors are reactive to the user's palette choice.
  # ----------------------------

  city_map_colors <- reactive({
    raw_palette <- access_map_palette_selected()
    if (is.function(raw_palette)) raw_palette(4) else brewer.pal(4, raw_palette)
  })

  # ── Shared tract map data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single source of truth for BOTH the interactive Leaflet map below and the
  # static print map built for the "Download Selected City" report
  # (render_city_tract_map() in scripts/functions.R, called from the download
  # handler further down). Both read this same joined, binned, colored data,
  # so the printed map can never land in a different bin or a different
  # colour than the one shown on screen. Was previously computed inline
  # inside output$snapshotmap only; pulled out so the download handler can
  # read it too without a second join-and-bin pass.
  city_map_data <- reactive({
    req(city_tract_sf(), city_tract())

    sf_df <- city_tract_sf() %>%
      mutate(tract_id_norm = normalize_tract_geoid(tract_GEOID))

    tab_df <- city_tract() %>%
      transmute(
        tract_id_norm = normalize_tract_geoid(GEOID),
        pct_cni_total_dis_place = pct_cni_total_dis_place   # already dbl 0–100
      )

    data <- left_join(sf_df, tab_df, by = "tract_id_norm")
    has_any_data <- any(!is.na(data$pct_cni_total_dis_place))

    map_colors   <- city_map_colors()
    map_na_color <- access_map_na_selected()

    data <- data %>%
      mutate(
        pct_cat = cut(
          pct_cni_total_dis_place,
          breaks         = city_map_breaks,
          include.lowest = TRUE,
          labels         = city_map_labels
        ),
        # No-data tracts take the no-data colour belonging to the SELECTED
        # palette, not a fixed grey. Under High Contrast Mono a grey would be
        # only 6.5 CIEDE2000 units from the lightest band, so "no data" would
        # read as "best". See the NO-DATA note in scripts/palettes.R.
        fill_col = dplyr::case_when(
          is.na(pct_cat) ~ map_na_color,
          TRUE           ~ map_colors[as.integer(pct_cat)]
        )
      )

    # Append a "No data" key ONLY when some tract actually lacks a value, so
    # the legend never explains a colour that is not on the map. This matters
    # more now that the no-data colour varies by palette: under High Contrast
    # Mono it is blue, which is unexplained otherwise.
    has_gaps   <- any(is.na(data$pct_cni_total_dis_place))
    leg_colors <- if (has_gaps) c(map_colors, map_na_color) else map_colors
    leg_labels <- if (has_gaps) c(city_map_labels, "No data") else city_map_labels

    list(
      data         = data,
      has_any_data = has_any_data,
      has_gaps     = has_gaps,
      leg_colors   = leg_colors,
      leg_labels   = leg_labels
    )
  })

  output$snapshotmap <- renderLeaflet({
    md   <- city_map_data()
    data <- md$data

    m <- leaflet(data) %>%
      # Muted, high-contrast neutral basemap (light gray / white) so the
      # tract choropleth does the color work and the map remains
      # accessible. CartoDB.Positron is WCAG-friendly and keeps labels
      # legible against any palette.
      addProviderTiles(
        providers$CartoDB.Positron,
        options = providerTileOptions(opacity = 0.9)
      ) %>%
      addResetMapButton() %>%
      addPolygons(
        stroke = TRUE, color = "#1c2b3a", weight = 1, smoothFactor = 0,
        fillColor = ~fill_col,
        fillOpacity = 0.82,
        layerId = ~tract_GEOID,
        label = ~lapply(ifelse(
          is.na(pct_cni_total_dis_place),
          paste0("<b>Tract ", tract_GEOID, "</b><br/>No data available"),
          paste0("<b>Tract ", tract_GEOID, "</b><br/>",
                 round(pct_cni_total_dis_place, 1), "% with disability")
        ), htmltools::HTML),
        labelOptions = labelOptions(
          style = list("font-weight" = "normal", padding = "3px 8px"),
          textsize = "13px",
          direction = "auto"
        ),
        highlight = highlightOptions(
          weight = 2.5,
          color = "#222222",
          fillOpacity = 0.95,
          bringToFront = TRUE
        )
      ) %>%
      addSearchOSM(
        options = searchOptions(
          autoCollapse = FALSE, minLength = 3, position = "topleft",
          zoom = 15, autoResize = FALSE, hideMarkerOnCollapse = TRUE
        )
      )
      # No addEasyprint() here. The map previously carried its own "Download
      # map as PNG" control; that affordance is now consolidated into the
      # single "Download Selected City" button in the controls card (see
      # output$download_city below), which produces the full branded,
      # accessible, print-ready report rather than a bare PNG of the map
      # alone. Per-map download intentionally removed, not just unused.

    if (md$has_any_data) {
      m <- m %>%
        addLegend(
          position = "topright",
          colors   = md$leg_colors,
          labels   = md$leg_labels,
          opacity  = 0.82,
          title    = "% With Disability"
        )
    } else {
      m <- m %>%
        addControl(
          html = paste0(
            "<div style='background: rgba(255,255,255,0.92); padding: 6px 8px; border-radius: 4px;'>",
            "<b>% With Disability</b><br/>No tract values joined (tract GEOID mismatch).",
            "</div>"
          ),
          position = "topright"
        )
    }

    m
  })

  # ----------------------------
  # City Summary Output
  # ----------------------------
  # ── Shared city profile bundle ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single source of truth for BOTH the on-screen summary card and the
  # downloadable full city report. Every fragment below (race_ethnicity,
  # sex, age_groups, ...) is built exactly once here via the same
  # render_demo_list() / render_comparison_table() helpers the page always
  # used, and both output$city_summary and the "Download Selected City"
  # handler read the same list, so the download can never drift from what is
  # on screen. Mirrors national_topic_bundle() in the National Data app above.
  city_download_bundle <- reactive({
    req(city_place())

    # Cleaned "City, State" title, shared by the map heading (output$city_map_title
    # applies the same transform separately) and this bundle's print title.
    full_title <- city_place() %>%
      mutate(NAME = str_replace_all(NAME, " (city|village|municipality|town), ", ", ")) %>%
      pull(NAME)

    introductory_text <- paste0(
      "Based on ACS 2024 5-Year Estimates, of the city's <b>", fmt_num(city_place()$pop_cni_total_all),
      "</b> residents, <b>", fmt_num(city_place()$pop_cni_total_dis_place),
      "</b> (<b>", fmt_pct_1dp(city_place()$pct_cni_total_dis_place), "</b>) are people with disabilities."
    )
    # The trailing <br><br> this string used to carry was spacing the lead
    # sentence off the block below it. Now that the sentence sits in its own
    # centred header, the paragraph margin handles that.

    # Explanatory / methodological notes, named once here rather than as
    # literals inside the paste0 assembly below, so the downloadable report
    # can quote the exact same sentences rather than a second hand-copied
    # version that could drift from the on-screen wording over time.
    #
    # Defined ahead of the section fragments rather than after them (where it
    # sat until 2026-08-18) because render_demo_list() now takes age_intro as
    # an argument, so the Age note travels inside the Age fragment to both
    # consumers instead of each one placing it separately.
    help <- list(
      demographics_intro = paste0(
        "For each Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age group below, the headline ",
        "figure is that group's share of the city's total population, with ",
        "the number of people that represents shown underneath it. ",
        "Hispanic/Latino is an ethnicity that can include people of any ",
        "race, so it overlaps with the race categories above it, and ",
        "figures across groups are not meant to sum to the city total."
      ),
      age_intro = paste0(
        "The Census asks about hearing and vision difficulty at every age, ",
        "but the other four disability types (cognitive, ambulatory, ",
        "self-care, and independent living) are only asked starting at age ",
        "5, and independent living only from age 15. The “Under 5” ",
        "figure below reflects hearing and vision difficulty alone, so it ",
        "is not directly comparable to the other age groups, which draw on ",
        "more disability types."
      ),
      disability_types_intro = paste0(
        "Each percentage below is the share of the city's total population, ",
        "not just the population with disabilities, that reports that ",
        "specific type of disability. A person can have more than one type, ",
        "and many do, so these categories overlap. The six figures below ",
        "will add up to more than the city's overall disability rate, often ",
        "to about twice it, and are not meant to sum to the total."
      ),
      outcomes_intro = paste0(
        "Each indicator below is shown for residents with disabilities ",
        "beside residents without disabilities, so the two can be compared ",
        "directly."
      ),
      health_insurance = paste0(
        "A person can hold public and private coverage at the same time, ",
        "so those two figures are not meant to sum to the any-coverage figure."
      ),
      earnings = paste0(
        "Median earnings in the past 12 months among residents ages 16 and ",
        "over who had earnings. This is pay from work only. It does not ",
        "include Social Security, disability benefits or investment income, ",
        "and it leaves out residents who did not work, so it is not a ",
        "measure of total income."
      ),
      poverty = paste0(
        "Living below the federal poverty line. As of 2024, that is a ",
        "yearly income below $14,891 for an individual or $29,678 for a ",
        "family of four."
      ),
      housing_burden = paste0(
        "Citywide figures for all households, not disability specific. A ",
        "disability specific breakdown is not published at the city level, ",
        "so there is no comparison to show here."
      ),
      housing_access = paste0(
        "Among households in each HUD-assisted housing program, the share ",
        "with a head of household or spouse/co-head who has a disability. ",
        "This is a rate within an already-assisted population, not a ",
        "citywide figure, so it should not be compared directly to the ",
        "disability rate shown elsewhere on this page. A missing figure ",
        "usually means the city has no households reported in that ",
        "program, not a suppressed or unpublished value."
      )
      # TEMPORARILY DISABLED 2026-08-17: paired with the cil_distance block
      # above. Re-enable once cil_weighted_mean_distance_mi is available.
      # ,
      # cil_distance = paste0(
      #   "The average straight-line distance a resident with a disability ",
      #   "would need to travel to reach the closest Center for Independent ",
      #   "Living, weighted by where people with disabilities live within ",
      #   "the city. This is straight-line distance, not travel time or a ",
      #   "road route. The nearest center by distance is not always the one ",
      #   "that serves this city: Centers for Independent Living have ",
      #   "defined service areas, usually by county or region."
      # )
    )

    race_ethnicity <- render_demo_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        demo_row("White alone (non-Hispanic)", "pop_cni_whitenonhisp_dis"),
        demo_row("Black/African American",     "pop_cni_black_dis"),
        demo_row("American Indian/Alaska Native", "pop_cni_aian_dis"),
        demo_row("Asian",                       "pop_cni_asian_dis"),
        demo_row("Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander", "pop_cni_nhopi_dis"),
        demo_row("Some other race(s) identified", "pop_cni_raceother_dis"),
        demo_row("Two or more races",           "pop_cni_racemulti_dis"),
        demo_row("Hispanic/Latino (any race)",  "pop_cni_hisp_dis")
      ),
      "Race / Ethnicity"
    )

    sex <- render_demo_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        demo_row("Male",   "pop_cni_male_dis"),
        demo_row("Female", "pop_cni_female_dis")
      ),
      "Sex"
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Age
    #
    # Same two-figure list as Race/Ethnicity and Sex, via render_demo_list():
    # count and share of the total population.
    #
    # Four bands, not three. An earlier version of this comment claimed
    # disability is "never recorded" under age 5 and dropped that band
    # entirely -- that was wrong. The ACS asks hearing and vision
    # difficulty at every age, including under 5; only the other four
    # types (cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, and independent living,
    # the last restricted to age 15+) start at age 5. Census still
    # publishes an official "has a disability" aggregate for under-5
    # children from the two types it does ask, and the pipeline carries
    # it as pop_cni_under5_dis_place, same numerator pattern as every
    # other band. Confirmed against city_place_full.Rds: the four bands
    # below sum exactly to pop_cni_total_dis_place for Los Angeles
    # (441,455 = 441,455); the three-band version was short by exactly
    # the under-5 count.
    #
    # Because the under-5 count is built from only 2 of the 6 disability
    # types while every other band draws on all 6 (or 5, for ages 5-14),
    # its share of the total population is not on the same footing as the
    # other bands -- a lower under-5 share does not mean disability is
    # rarer at that age, only that fewer question types apply. The help
    # text below the list says so.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    age_groups <- render_demo_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        demo_row("Under 5",            "pop_cni_under5_dis_place"),
        demo_row("Ages 5 to 17",       "pop_cni_5to17_dis_place"),
        demo_row("Ages 18 to 64",      "pop_cni_18to64_dis_place"),
        demo_row("Ages 65 and older",  "pop_cni_65plus_dis_place")
      ),
      "Age",
      # Sits between the "Age" heading and the tiles. It used to be emitted
      # separately by each consumer, above the heading, where it read as a
      # closing note on Sex rather than an introduction to Age.
      note = help$age_intro
    )

    # Stat tiles, matching Race/Ethnicity, Sex and Age, per Colin's
    # 2026-08-18 request. The returned fragment is a complete
    # <ul class="city-demo-list">, so neither consumer wraps it in a <ul>
    # of its own any more. Labels keep the parenthetical plain-language
    # gloss that the bullet version carried.
    disability_types <- render_type_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        type_row("Hearing",
                 "pop_cni_total_hearing_dis",   "pct_cni_total_hearing_dis"),
        type_row("Vision",
                 "pop_cni_total_vision_dis",    "pct_cni_total_vision_dis"),
        type_row("Cognitive",
                 "pop_cni_total_cognitive_dis", "pct_cni_total_cognitive_dis"),
        type_row("Ambulatory (difficulty walking or climbing stairs)",
                 "pop_cni_total_mobility_dis",  "pct_cni_total_mobility_dis"),
        type_row("Self Care (difficulty bathing or dressing)",
                 "pop_cni_selfcare_dis",        "pct_cni_selfcare_dis"),
        type_row("Independent Living (difficulty doing errands alone)",
                 "pop_cni_indepliving_dis",     "pct_cni_indepliving_dis")
      )
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Outcome indicators, paired with/without disability
    #
    # From here to the housing-burden block, every indicator is rendered as a
    # two-column comparison table via render_comparison_table(). cp is the
    # single-row city data frame the specs read from.
    #
    # Housing cost burden is the one exception and stays a bullet list: it
    # comes from B25070 and B25091, which are household tables with no
    # disability dimension, so there is no comparison to draw.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    cp <- city_place()

    employment <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Employed, part or full time",
                "pct_cni_18to64_employed_dis",   "pct_cni_18to64_employed_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_employed_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_employed_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Unemployed, looking for work",
                "pct_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis", "pct_cni_18to64_nodis_unemployed",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Out of the labor force",
                "pct_cni_18to64_notlabor_dis",   "pct_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_notlabor_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis")
      ),
      "Labor force status, ages 18 to 64"
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Earnings
    #
    # ACS B18140. Note the dictionary calls these variables "Median
    # Individual Income", but B18140 measures median EARNINGS, meaning pay
    # from work only, over a universe restricted to people who had
    # earnings. It excludes benefits, Social Security, SSI and investment
    # income, so it is not individual income in the ordinary sense. The
    # labels below say earnings; the dictionary entry should be corrected
    # to match.
    #
    # Coverage: the disabled figure resolves for 4,821 of the 5,881
    # non-CDP places in the selector, and the non-disabled figure is
    # present for all but two of those, so the pair travels together.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    earnings <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Median earnings, ages 16 and over",
                "pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis", "pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis",
                kind = "dollar")
      ),
      "Median earnings among residents who had earnings"
    )

    poverty <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Children under 18",
                "pct_cni_under18_poverty_dis", "pct_cni_under18_poverty_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_under18_poverty_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_under18_poverty_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Adults 18 to 64",
                "pct_cni_18to64_poverty_dis",  "pct_cni_18to64_poverty_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_poverty_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_poverty_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Adults 65 and older",
                "pct_cni_65plus_poverty_dis",  "pct_cni_65plus_poverty_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_65plus_poverty_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_65plus_poverty_nodis")
      ),
      "Residents living below the federal poverty line"
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Health insurance, split by age band
    #
    # The 19-64 band was already shown. The 65+ band is the same four
    # measures and is populated for 8,372 of 8,407 places, so it is shown
    # alongside rather than gated. "Any coverage" is listed first because
    # private and public overlap and will not sum to it.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Both age bands use the same four measures, so the spec is built once and
    # the column prefix is swapped. "nodis" sits in the middle of these names,
    # which is why the pairs are assembled here rather than derived.
    health_insurance_rows <- function(band) {
      list(
        cmp_row("Any health insurance coverage",
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_dis_healthins"),
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_nodis_healthins"),
                dis_pop   = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_dis_healthins"),
                nodis_pop = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_nodis_healthins")),
        cmp_row("Private health insurance",
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_dis_privatehealth"),
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_nodis_privatehealth"),
                dis_pop   = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_dis_privatehealth"),
                nodis_pop = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_nodis_privatehealth")),
        cmp_row("Public health insurance",
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_dis_publichealth"),
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_nodis_publichealth"),
                dis_pop   = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_dis_publichealth"),
                nodis_pop = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_nodis_publichealth")),
        cmp_row("No health insurance",
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_dis_nohealthins"),
                paste0("pct_cni_", band, "_nodis_nohealthins"),
                dis_pop   = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_dis_nohealthins"),
                nodis_pop = paste0("pop_cni_", band, "_nodis_nohealthins"))
      )
    }

    health_insurance_19to64 <- render_comparison_table(
      cp, health_insurance_rows("19to64"), "Ages 19 to 64"
    )

    health_insurance_65plus <- render_comparison_table(
      cp, health_insurance_rows("65plus"), "Ages 65 and older"
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Education and Transportation, both from ACS S1811
    #
    # S1811 is published only where the population with disabilities clears a
    # threshold between 7,178 and 7,883 residents, which is 694 of the 8,407
    # places in the file and 648 of the 5,881 selectable non-CDP places. The
    # non-NA set is byte-identical across all five S1811-derived measures, so
    # one sentinel gates both blocks.
    #
    # Rather than render two blocks of "Not available" for nearly nine cities
    # in ten, has_s1811 hides them and the assembly substitutes a sentence
    # naming the reason. Before this, the page footnote attributed the gaps to
    # a population threshold of 30,000, which is measurably wrong: 1,322
    # selectable cities exceed that population but only 648 carry the data.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    has_s1811 <- !is.na(cp$pct_cni_25plus_noGED_dis)

    education <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Less than high school",
                "pct_cni_25plus_noGED_dis",     "pct_cni_25plus_noGED_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_25plus_noGED_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_25plus_noGED_nodis"),
        cmp_row("High school diploma or equivalent",
                "pct_cni_25plus_GED_dis",       "pct_cni_25plus_GED_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_25plus_GED_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_25plus_GED_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Bachelor's degree or higher",
                "pct_cni_25plus_bachelors_dis", "pct_cni_25plus_bachelors_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_25plus_bachelors_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_25plus_bachelors_nodis")
      ),
      "Highest level of education completed, ages 25 and over"
    )

    transportation <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Commute to work by public transit",
                "pct_cni_16plus_transit_dis",    "pct_cni_16plus_transit_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_16plus_transit_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_16plus_transit_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Commute to work driving alone",
                "pct_cni_16plus_drivealone_dis", "pct_cni_16plus_drivealone_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_16plus_drivealone_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_16plus_drivealone_nodis")
      ),
      "Commute mode among workers ages 16 and over"
    )

    # Substituted for both blocks when the city has no S1811 data.
    s1811_unavailable_note <- paste0(
      '<p class="city-summary-help">Education and commuting figures are not ',
      'published for this city. The Census releases these measures only where ',
      'the population with disabilities is large enough, roughly 7,500 ',
      'residents, which covers 648 of the cities in this tool.</p>'
    )

    housing_burden <- city_place() %>%
      transmute(
        `Renter households paying 30% or more of income on rent` =
          create_number_percent_string(total_rent_burdened, pct_rent_burdened),
        `Households with a mortgage paying 30% or more of income on housing` =
          create_number_percent_string(mortgage_burdened_households, pct_households_mortgage_burdened)
      ) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Indicator", values_to = "Value (%)") %>%
      mutate(Bullets = paste0("<li>", Indicator, " &mdash; ", `Value (%)`, "</li>")) %>%
      pull(Bullets) %>%
      str_c(collapse = "")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Housing Access (HUD POSH), Community Living domain
    #
    # pct_cni_hoh_hcv_dis and pct_cni_hoh_pubhousing_dis are joined onto
    # city_place_full.Rds in city_transform_final.R from the HUD Picture of
    # Subsidized Households place file. Same source and same variable names
    # as the national/scorecard "Housing Access" index (see ind_src below),
    # now also live at city geography.
    #
    # No with/without-disability comparison here, same reason as Housing
    # Cost Burden: the measure is the share of an already HUD-assisted
    # population whose head has a disability, not a citywide rate, so there
    # is no non-disability denominator to pair it against. Bullet list, not
    # render_comparison_table().
    #
    # A missing value is common and expected: it means the city has no
    # reported households in that specific program (2,111 of 8,407 cities
    # have Public Housing data; 5,920 have Housing Choice Voucher data),
    # not a suppressed or unpublished figure.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    housing_access <- city_place() %>%
      transmute(
        `Housing Choice Vouchers` = fmt_pct_or_na(pct_cni_hoh_hcv_dis),
        `Public Housing`          = fmt_pct_or_na(pct_cni_hoh_pubhousing_dis)
      ) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Program", values_to = "Value") %>%
      mutate(Bullets = paste0("<li>", Program, " &mdash; ", Value, "</li>")) %>%
      pull(Bullets) %>%
      str_c(collapse = "")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Distance to nearest Center for Independent Living, Community
    # Participation domain (Access to Resources).
    #
    # TEMPORARILY DISABLED 2026-08-17: cil_weighted_mean_distance_mi is not
    # yet joined onto city_place_full.Rds (pipeline step not finished),
    # which threw "object 'cil_weighted_mean_distance_mi' not found" in
    # city_place() %>% transmute(). Re-enable this block, the cil_distance
    # entry in the help list below, and the "Access to Resources" markup in
    # city_summary_tables once the CIL join lands in the pipeline repo.
    #
    # cil_weighted_mean_distance_mi, cil_nearest_center_name and
    # cil_nearest_center_distance_mi are joined onto city_place_full.Rds in
    # city_transform_final.R from the ACL SILC/CIL list
    # (analysis/data/cil_centers.csv), geocoded and reduced to straight-line
    # distances by transformCityCilData() in the pipeline repo.
    #
    # No with/without-disability comparison: like Housing Access, this is a
    # place-level measure (distance from the city to a resource), not a
    # person-level rate, so there is no non-disability denominator to pair
    # it against. Bullet list, not render_comparison_table().
    #
    # Unlike Housing Access, coverage here is close to 100% -- straight-line
    # distance is always computable, so "Not available" would mean a data
    # problem upstream, not an expected gap the way a missing HUD program is.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # cil_distance <- city_place() %>%
    #   transmute(
    #     `Average Distance to Nearest Center` =
    #       fmt_miles_or_na(cil_weighted_mean_distance_mi),
    #     `Nearest Center` = ifelse(
    #       is.na(cil_nearest_center_name),
    #       "Not available",
    #       paste0(
    #         cil_nearest_center_name, " (",
    #         fmt_miles_or_na(cil_nearest_center_distance_mi), ")"
    #       )
    #     )
    #   ) %>%
    #   tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Value") %>%
    #   mutate(Bullets = paste0("<li>", Measure, " &mdash; ", Value, "</li>")) %>%
    #   pull(Bullets) %>%
    #   str_c(collapse = "")

    # Scoped to living arrangements only now that Housing Access is live.
    # Do not fold Housing Access back into this note; the two are shown as
    # separate subsections below.
    community_living_note <- paste0(
      '<p class="city-summary-help">Living arrangement measures, covering ',
      'whether people with disabilities live at home, in non-institutional ',
      'group quarters, or in a nursing home or correctional facility, are ',
      'not available for individual cities. The Census publishes the ',
      'underlying tables (S2601A, S2602, B26108) only for the nation, ',
      'states and larger regions, so these measures appear on the National ',
      'Data tab rather than here. This is a limit in how the Census ',
      'releases group quarters data, not a gap in this pipeline. A partial ',
      'estimate for the largest cities, built from Census microdata, is ',
      'under development for a future update.</p>'
    )


    city_summary_tables <- paste0(

      # ── Shared heading, centred above both columns ──────────────────────────
      '<div class="row">',
      '<div class="col-md-12">',
      '<div class="city-summary-header">',
      '<h3>People with Disabilities - Summary Tables</h3>',
      '<p>', introductory_text, '</p>',
      '</div>',
      '</div>',
      '</div>',

      # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
      # Row two. Who has disabilities in this city. ONE full-width card.
      #
      # Demographics and Disability Types share a single card rather than
      # sitting in two columns. Split across two columns the types list, at
      # six items, left a large block of dead space beside the much longer
      # demographics list. One wide card carries both, and everything inside
      # it stacks in a single vertical column at every width.
      #
      # Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age render as grids of stat tiles via
      # render_demo_list(): share of the total population as the headline
      # figure with the count beneath, per the client's 2026-08-18 request
      # to simplify away from the earlier four-column tables. No
      # without-disability column: the paired with/without comparisons all
      # live in row three.
      # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
      '<div class="row" style="margin-top:1.25rem;">',
      '<div class="col-md-12">',
      '<div class="city-summary city-summary-wide">',

      '<h4>Disability Demographics</h4>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$demographics_intro, '</p>',
      race_ethnicity,
      sex,
      # age_groups now carries help$age_intro itself, between the "Age"
      # heading and the tiles. It used to be emitted here, above the
      # heading, where it read as a note on Sex.
      age_groups,

      '<h4>Disability Types</h4>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$disability_types_intro, '</p>',
      # A complete <ul class="city-demo-list"> of stat tiles since
      # 2026-08-18, not bullets, so no wrapping <ul> here.
      disability_types,

      '</div>',   # end .city-summary
      '</div>',   # end .col-md-12
      '</div>',   # end .row

      # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
      # Row three. Outcomes, grouped by ADA-PARC domain.
      #
      # The domain each block sits in is taken from data/dict_vars.csv rather
      # than chosen here: the health insurance, education and transportation
      # variables all carry is_community_participation, and the employment,
      # earnings, poverty and housing burden variables all carry
      # is_work_economic. Housing cost burden reads as a community living
      # measure but the dictionary classes it as economic, so that is where
      # it sits.
      #
      # Every block is a paired comparison table except Housing Cost Burden,
      # which has no disability dimension in B25070 or B25091.
      #
      # One full-width card per domain, stacked, since 2026-08-18. The two
      # domains used to sit side by side in col-md-6 halves, which put four
      # or five comparison tables into each half at roughly half the
      # readable width and made the strip below the map dense and wide.
      # Stacking them matches the downloadable report's single-column flow
      # and lets the tables carry a larger type size (see the
      # .city-summary-stack rules in the stylesheet). The equal-height
      # .city-summary-row class is gone with the halves: nothing sits beside
      # anything now, so there is no ragged edge to even out.
      # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
      '<div class="row" style="margin-top:0.25rem;">',

      '<div class="col-md-12">',
      '<div class="city-summary city-summary-stack">',
      '<h4>Community Participation</h4>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$outcomes_intro, '</p>',
      '<b>Health Insurance</b>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$health_insurance, '</p>',
      health_insurance_19to64,
      health_insurance_65plus,

      # Education and Transportation share the S1811 publication ceiling, so
      # both are replaced by one explanatory sentence when it is not met.
      if (has_s1811) {
        paste0(
          '<b>Education</b>',
          education,
          '<b>Transportation</b>',
          transportation
        )
      } else {
        paste0('<b>Education and Transportation</b>', s1811_unavailable_note)
      },

      # TEMPORARILY DISABLED 2026-08-17: cil_distance / help$cil_distance
      # are commented out above until the CIL join lands in the pipeline.
      # '<b>Access to Resources</b>',
      # '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$cil_distance, '</p>',
      # '<ul>', cil_distance, '</ul>',

      '</div>',   # end .city-summary
      '</div>',   # end .col-md-12

      '<div class="col-md-12">',
      '<div class="city-summary city-summary-stack">',
      '<h4>Work and Economic</h4>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$outcomes_intro, '</p>',
      '<b>Employment</b>',
      employment,
      '<b>Earnings</b>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$earnings, '</p>',
      earnings,
      '<b>Poverty</b>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$poverty, '</p>',
      poverty,
      '<b>Housing Cost Burden</b>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$housing_burden, '</p>',
      '<ul>', housing_burden, '</ul>',
      '</div>',   # end .city-summary
      '</div>',   # end .col-md-12

      '</div>',   # end .row

      # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
      # Row four. Community Living, the fourth ADA-PARC domain.
      #
      # Housing Access (HUD POSH) is live at city geography as of 12 August
      # 2026 -- see city_import_hud.R / transformCityHudData.R in the
      # pipeline repo. Living arrangement measures (home, group quarters,
      # nursing home, corrections) are still not: the underlying Census
      # tables (S2601A, S2602, B26108) publish only for the nation, states
      # and larger regions. community_living_note covers only that
      # remaining gap now; do not fold Housing Access back into it. A
      # PUMS-based partial estimate for large cities is a candidate for a
      # future update (see the 9 August 2026 city data indicator status
      # review, table four, item 6); do not claim it is live until it ships.
      # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
      '<div class="row" style="margin-top:0.25rem;">',
      '<div class="col-md-12">',
      '<div class="city-summary city-summary-note">',
      '<h4>Community Living</h4>',

      '<b>Housing Access</b>',
      '<p class="city-summary-help">', help$housing_access, '</p>',
      '<ul>', housing_access, '</ul>',

      community_living_note,
      '</div>',   # end .city-summary
      '</div>',   # end .col-md-12
      '</div>'    # end .row
    )

    # ── Scalars and map pieces, for the print banner/title/headline and the
    # static map on the download, which need these as plain values rather
    # than pre-assembled screen HTML. ────────────────────────────────────────
    city_label  <- sub(",.*$", "", full_title)
    state_label <- input$state_selector %||% sub("^.*,\\s*", "", full_title)

    md <- city_map_data()

    list(
      # Identity / headline
      city_label   = city_label,
      state_label  = state_label,
      full_title   = full_title,
      intro_text   = introductory_text,
      source_note  = "Based on 2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates",
      # "generated" is deliberately NOT set here: this reactive also feeds the
      # on-screen card, where a generation date is meaningless, and the
      # download handler below sets it fresh at click time (matching
      # national_topic_bundle(), which carries no "generated" field for the
      # same reason). Setting it in both places would leave two list entries
      # named "generated" once the handler splices this bundle together with
      # its own, and $ / [[ silently return only the first.

      # Map
      map_data     = md$data,
      map_alt_text = cityMapAltText(md$data, city_label),
      leg_colors   = md$leg_colors,
      leg_labels   = md$leg_labels,

      # Section fragments, reused verbatim by both the on-screen card and the
      # downloadable report so the two can never disagree.
      race_ethnicity          = race_ethnicity,
      sex                     = sex,
      age_groups              = age_groups,
      disability_types        = disability_types,
      employment              = employment,
      earnings                = earnings,
      poverty                 = poverty,
      health_insurance_19to64 = health_insurance_19to64,
      health_insurance_65plus = health_insurance_65plus,
      has_s1811               = has_s1811,
      education               = education,
      transportation          = transportation,
      s1811_unavailable_note  = s1811_unavailable_note,
      housing_burden          = housing_burden,
      housing_access          = housing_access,
      community_living_note   = community_living_note,
      help                    = help,

      # Full assembled on-screen HTML (unchanged from the original inline
      # build), kept here so output$city_summary below stays a one-line
      # consumer of this bundle.
      city_summary_tables = city_summary_tables
    )
  })

  output$city_summary <- renderUI({
    HTML(city_download_bundle()$city_summary_tables)
  })

  # ── Download Selected City: full branded, print-ready HTML report ────────
  # Renders city/city_profile.qmd for the current selection into a
  # self-contained ADA-PARC branded HTML: banner, static tract map + key,
  # then the same summary tables shown on screen. All content is prepared
  # here and passed via an RDS bundle so the download always matches the
  # on-screen city summary. Mirrors the National Data "Download Selected
  # Topic" handler above.
  city_app_root <- normalizePath(
    getOption("shiny.appdir", default = getwd()),
    mustWork = FALSE
  )
  city_dir     <- file.path(city_app_root, "city")
  city_qmd     <- file.path(city_dir, "city_profile.qmd")
  city_out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "ada_parc_city_dl")
  dir.create(city_out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  output$download_city <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
      b    <- city_download_bundle()
      slug <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", paste0(b$city_label, "_", b$state_label))
      slug <- gsub("^_|_$", "", slug)
      paste0("ADAPARC_", slug, "_Profile_2024.html")
    },
    content = function(file) {
      withProgress(
        message = "Building your ADA-PARC city report…",
        detail  = "This usually takes 20–35 seconds.",
        value   = 0.15,
        {
          b <- city_download_bundle()

          # Static counterpart to the Leaflet map, built from the exact same
          # binned/colored data (see city_map_data() above), exported to
          # inline SVG the same way the National Data download exports its
          # ggiraph map. svglite emits font-family="EB Garamond"; the browser
          # pairs it with the webfont loaded via font-loader.html.
          gg <- render_city_tract_map(b$map_data)
          svg_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
          ggplot2::ggsave(
            filename = svg_tmp, plot = gg,
            device = svglite::svglite,
            width = 7.5, height = 7, bg = "white"
          )
          map_svg <- paste(readLines(svg_tmp, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
          unlink(svg_tmp)

          setProgress(0.4, detail = "Composing the document…")

          # map_data (the sf object) is dropped: the qmd only ever needs the
          # rendered map_svg, and RDS-ing an sf object across the separate
          # quarto render process is weight the download does not need.
          out_bundle <- c(
            b[setdiff(names(b), "map_data")],
            list(map_svg = map_svg, generated = format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y"))
          )
          bundle_path <- file.path(city_out_dir, "bundle.rds")
          saveRDS(out_bundle, bundle_path)

          setProgress(0.55, detail = "Rendering HTML…")

          tryCatch({
            quarto::quarto_render(
              input          = city_qmd,
              execute_params = list(bundle = bundle_path),
              execute_dir    = city_dir
            )
            rendered <- file.path(city_dir, "city_profile.html")
            if (file.exists(rendered)) {
              file.copy(rendered, file, overwrite = TRUE)
            } else {
              writeLines("<html><body>Report could not be generated.</body></html>", file)
            }
            setProgress(1)
          }, error = function(e) {
            showNotification(
              ui       = paste("Download failed:", conditionMessage(e)),
              type     = "error",
              duration = 15
            )
            writeLines(
              paste0("<html><body>Report could not be generated: ",
                     htmltools::htmlEscape(conditionMessage(e)), "</body></html>"),
              file
            )
          })
        }
      )
    }
  )
}

# Run the app
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```{r scorecard_new, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(shiny)

# ── Resolve app root to an absolute path ───────────────────────────────────
# getOption("shiny.appdir") is set by rmarkdown::run() to the .Rmd's directory,
# so this works whether the app is launched from RStudio, the R console, or
# shinyapps.io. Falls back to getwd() as a safety net.
app_root <- normalizePath(
  getOption("shiny.appdir", default = getwd()),
  mustWork = FALSE
)

# ── Path to the scorecard directory ────────────────────────────────────────
# All data files, dictionaries, and .qmd templates are copied here from the
# data pipeline repo (ADAPARCDataPipeline/scorecard_quarto) so that the app
# is self-contained and deploys correctly to shinyapps.io.
# To update: re-run the data pipeline and copy the new index_scores_wide.csv
# into scorecard/scorecard_data/final/, then copy the updated .qmd files too.
scorecard_dir <- file.path(app_root, "scorecard")

# ── Output directory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Rendered scorecard HTML is written to a per-process temp directory so
# stale files are never bundled into the deployment (the old www/ approach
# caused pre-deployment renders to be served on the live site even after
# the QMD templates were updated).  A unique dir per process avoids cross-
# session collisions on multi-worker deployments.
sc_out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "ada_parc_sc_out")
dir.create(sc_out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
shiny::addResourcePath("sc_out", sc_out_dir)

  read_csv(file.path(scorecard_dir, "dictionary/scorecard_indicator_dictionary.csv"),
           show_col_types = FALSE),
  error = function(e) { warning("Could not load indicator dictionary: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL }
)

           show_col_types = FALSE),

  raw <- read_csv(file.path(scorecard_dir, "scorecard_data/final/index_scores_wide.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
  df  <- raw |>
    filter(ABBR != "USA", !is.na(NAME), !is.na(ABBR)) |>
    mutate(NAME = as.character(NAME), ABBR = as.character(ABBR)) |>
    arrange(NAME)
  setNames(df$ABBR, df$NAME)
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("Could not read data file for state list: ", conditionMessage(e))
  c("Illinois" = "IL", "New York" = "NY", "California" = "CA")
})
```
